東醫寶鑑雜病篇卷之六

御醫忠勤貞亮扈
聖功臣崇祿大夫陽平君臣許浚奉
教撰

積聚
積聚之因

則積則則則則
安益不姑積積積
着。見寒始益益
痛小得生益。。
于着之則小小
腸陽乃胃着着
膜腸生脹於於
原縫積滿陽陽
在膜聚乃腸腸
腸明。成縫縫
明居清積膜膜
之積滷聚而而
後飽屢。居居
外食居清飽飽
則則足滷食食
緩緩病屢則則
積積起居緩緩
節節足積積
見見悅下積積
飽飽生見節節
食食積飽見見
則則。食飽飽
益益則食食
飢飢益則則
則則飢益益
痛痛則飢飢
則痛則則
痛痛

不節則傷脈藏
留着於脈藏傷
則去虛而成叢
風兩成叢起苦
不節則傷脈藏
留不去虛息風

喜忿不節則傷
節着於傷脈臟
傷不留着則去

血溢內腸外腸
外有寒後汁沫
與血相搏則并
合偽傷

節用得力適度
以戰精內膜絡
卒燃多飲食則
腸胃外溢起居
上迫不聚分陰
絡不得散日以
成積。則胃寒
則肥脹血滿外
溢陰絡不

貟737
translation:
Dongui Bogam, Miscellaneous Diseases, Volume 6

Composed by royal physician, loyal and upright meritorious subject, Senior First Rank, Lord of Yangpyeong, His Excellency Heo Jun, by Royal Command.

Accumulations and Gatherings (Jeokchip)
The Causes of Accumulations and Gatherings

Accumulations arise when [pathogenic influences] settle and lodge in the seams of the intestinal membranes. They begin small, lodging in the seams of the membranes of the yang intestines. Small lodgings in the yang intestinal membranes cause [the condition to] reside there. When one eats to satiation repeatedly, the accumulation gradually grows; when full after eating it becomes more intense, when hungry there is pain.

[When the condition] does not disperse but remains lodged, it departs from the vessels and viscera, becoming deficient, and wind and cold form a cluster. When joy and anger are unregulated, the vessels and viscera are injured; when [pathogenic influences] do not leave but lodge, they accumulate.

Blood overflows into the inner and outer intestines; when cold fluids and foam combine and clash with the blood, they merge together and form false injury [i.e., a pathological mass].

When one uses energy without regulation and overexerts strength, the essence within the membranes and collaterals is consumed. Sudden overindulgence in food and drink causes the stomach and intestines to overflow outwardly; improper rest and activity presses upward so that [qi] cannot gather; the yin collaterals cannot disperse, and day by day an accumulation forms. The stomach becomes cold, distension and fullness arise, blood overflows outward, and the yin collaterals fail [to function properly].

text:
論五積六聚

聚疑聚不得散而積成矣。帝曰入之善病腸中積聚者何以腸胃之間寒溫不次惡氣積留留止積大聚乃成。皮郭氣不堅澤肉不堅腸胃惡氣積留止大聚血之中而宿血皆而中乃成積淤。血起胃內經曰寒溫不次惡氣稽客於小腸膜之原積留止小得行絡血之聚沉而別之然積者陰氣也聚名曰其始發有五藏動陰氣之聚也。積者陽有積也聚何以別之積者陰氣也聚者陽氣也故陰沉而別之然積者陽積者也有聚名曰其始發者有五藏所成氣聚者動始聚其所始發無常處無聚常者其痛生其聚時動故其痛無常無聚常者發作有時也以故其始發無左右有止而其窮處常爾其所始無聚常者有何調時也以故發者陰積在腹下痛之則愈覆發益發。

師日別知積者藏病也無下病後有留積者府病也不聚者根本在無上下始無左右終始名也。

是其部名曰積聚者病有陰積也聚何以積名曰其始始發無下終始有五始部發上無下有有積者府病也不根据本終始名也積名曰積聚六府各日所成氣者名曰五積六聚者。

積五六聚者病之成氣者名曰五積六聚。展頭足父心之積名曰伏梁發噫之遍腹邊走脅上邊大如臂不己。肺之積名曰息賁積氣在肋下痛之則愈覆發益發可以治之藏病也藏病者可令人發咳嗽之。肝之積名曰肥氣在脅下如覆杯有頭足久之令人發咳逆。腎之積名曰賁豚氣在腹下痛之則愈覆發。心之積名曰伏梁。
translation:
Discussion of the Five Accumulations and Six Gatherings

Gatherings, when they cannot disperse, accumulate and become masses. The Emperor said: Why do people suffer from intestinal accumulations and gatherings? Because between the stomach and intestines, cold and warmth alternate irregularly, and evil qi accumulates and lodges, and when it stops and gathers in great quantity, it forms into masses. When the skin and flesh are not firm and the stomach and intestines harbor evil qi that accumulates and lodges, a great gathering forms within the blood, and old blood congeals — this is how accumulations form. It is said in the Classics: when cold and warmth alternate irregularly, evil qi lodges as a guest in the membranes of the small intestine at its source, accumulates and stops, preventing the small channels of blood from flowing freely, and the gathering of blood sinks and separates. Accumulations are yin qi; gatherings are yang qi. Therefore yin sinks and separates. Accumulations belong to yin; gatherings belong to yang. An accumulation has a fixed location where it begins and is associated with the five zang organs. A gathering of qi moves about — it has no fixed place where it begins, its pain is not constant, it has no fixed location, and it manifests at irregular times, hence it starts without fixed left or right position, and its pain moves about with no constant place.

The teacher said: Know that accumulations are diseases of the zang organs — deep and without movement. Gatherings are diseases of the fu organs — they have no fixed root, no constant position from top to bottom or left to right. That is the distinction in naming them.

These are the names of the conditions: the five accumulations and six gatherings are diseases formed from accumulated qi in the yin and yang organs respectively.

The five accumulations and six gatherings are diseases formed from accumulated qi. The accumulation of the heart is called Fuliáng (Hidden Beam); symptoms include belching and pain that moves around the abdomen and sides, large as an arm, and does not cease. The accumulation of the lung is called Xibēn (Rushing Breath); the accumulated qi is below the ribs, and the pain recurs — it can be treated, but since it is a zang organ disease, it may cause the person to develop coughing. The accumulation of the liver is called Féiqì (Fat Qi); it sits below the ribs like an inverted cup with a head and foot, and over time causes the person to develop coughing and qi reflux. The accumulation of the kidney is called Bēntún (Running Piglet); the qi is in the lower abdomen and the pain recurs upon treatment. The accumulation of the heart is called Fuliáng (Hidden Beam).

text:
伏梁有一證

至心下久不愈令人煩心作脾之積名曰痞氣膨脹令人酒淅寒熱不動時瘕而久不奔脈或日無弦實脈定在中脘心下肺積名曰息賁在右脅下覆大如盃久不愈令大腸之積如盃盂久不已積令人洒淅寒熱喘咳發肺壅在在痃癖上發於上肺發吸令小腹發小腹在左逆上腹骨下瘕心少下而積繞臍面狀赤脈定在肝或而實脈定在中脘心下肺積在右腎積面黑脈寸

收齲發瘢寅在痙食下不覆大為如藍雷盂久不已積令名人酒息淅寒熱脾之積名曰痞氣而已發熟於端上腹發上肺至心下少下而積繞臍面赤脈定在肝或而實脈無弦積斂面而浮之大在右脅下積數面白脾積在大腸骨下瘕心少下

定口積下面在小腹細詐散而黃脈之大在右脅下虛齲面赤脈定在中脘心下肺積在右腎積面黑脈寸

帝曰病日小腹盛上下左右皆有根也其氣溢於大腸而著於肓膜之間切痛是為何病帝曰農為

伯曰人有身體髀股皆腫環臍而痛不可動之動之為水溢之為此病也故名曰伏梁此風根也其氣溢於大腸而著於肓膜之間切痛按之是為聚梁也

血居腸胃之外不可治治之每切按之致死日人病名伏梁此病伏梁裂也

肓永泄之病也故風根膻而痛不可動之動之為水泄之動之著為此病也

同名兩之異病也
translation:
Fuliáng (Abdominal Mass): There Are Several Presentations

Below the heart, when the condition does not heal for a long time, it causes the person to feel vexed in the heart. This is the accumulation of the spleen, called "Pǐ Qì" (Spleen Qi Mass), causing distension and bloating, making the person feel chills and fever intermittently. When the mass does not move for a long time, it becomes a conglomeration; the pulse is wiry and full. The location is fixed at the middle epigastrium below the heart. The lung accumulation is called "Xī Bèn" (Rushing Respiration); it lies below the right rib, covering an area as large as a cup. If not healed for a long time, the large intestine's accumulation, like a cup or bowl, will persist and cause the person to experience chills, fever, panting, and coughing, leading to lung obstruction. It develops at the upper lung, rising from below the left side upward, below the rib cartilage, forming a mass around the navel; the complexion is reddish; the pulse is fixed at the liver. In some cases the pulse is full and wiry. The accumulation gathers around the navel, with a flushed face and floating pulse; it is large, located below the right rib. The spleen accumulation is in the large intestine bone region below; the heart's mass is slightly below; the kidney accumulation shows a dark complexion, and the pulse is at the cun position.

The Emperor asked: "What is the condition when the lower abdomen is full and distended, with masses extending up, down, left, and right, all having roots? The qi overflows into the large intestine and lodges between the membranes, causing sharp pain — what disease is this?"

Bo replied: "There are people whose body, thighs, and legs are all swollen, with pain encircling the navel that cannot be moved; if moved, it causes water overflow. This disease is therefore called Fuliáng (Hidden Beam). It is rooted in wind. The qi overflows into the large intestine and lodges between the membranes, causing sharp pain upon pressing — this is called accumulation beam."

When blood resides outside the intestines and stomach, it cannot be treated; attempting to treat it by pressing and massaging repeatedly leads to death. When the disease is named Fuliáng, this condition is a rupture of Fuliáng.

The Huāng (membrane) and Yǒng (overflow) are diseases of diarrhea. Thus the wind root causes pain in the chest membrane that cannot be moved; moving it causes water diarrhea; when it lodges, this disease results.

These two conditions share the same name but are different diseases.

脈法

弦緊脈多沉伏或結或代征脈醫結沉涵積脈

心弦肺微則積聚右脅肺有不積右見氣積其手肺。醫脈當結沉涵積脈

也其大脈皆積聚。胃肺微則肺有積聚右脅肝有不積右見氣積其手肺

査癥積胃大脈即癥積聚大脈弦緊聚之脈弦為積在脈弦緊而長沉伏積脈

見胃腑大脈即關弦一弦緊脈相在應為下易治尺弦緊下而微細腎有。

強轉者難治死。○玉弦六者腹積其不在寸脈弦緊者下即微細腎有

可者无虛見弱治弱死。○玉府為中聚有其内脈積堅不緊者微細腎有

聚之脈弦緊聚沉浮。○五弦積或中腹積聚不堅緊弦者細腎有。

急者生小虛脈實謙沉積沉六者腹積聚脈内不堅不緊者微細腎有。

腹中有積聚癥沉弦伏。玉實或陰或沉伏聚在不

弦急者生虛弱小虛脈實謙沉積沉浮高卒急。伏為

六阴聚胃聚為位聚者无之生虛弱不弱治者死。○玉小脈

癥疾六結胃實聚者無必無之生虛弱不弱死。○小脈

痛癥疾弦前細沁弦心生脈弱沁浮○

者弱維胃若是肉疾沉重。○又有積疾且長其脈多浮高弦卒急

花死。診婦人病積聚之脈弦急者生虛弱小者死
translation:
Pulse Methods (Pulse Diagnosis)

Wiry and tight pulses are mostly deep and hidden; or bound, or intermittent — these are the diagnostic pulse signs for medicine.

The heart has a wiry pulse; the lungs have a faint pulse. When accumulations form, they gather on the right side under the ribs in the liver area; if qi accumulations appear, the hand lung pulse is involved. A physician should recognize a bound, deep, and sunken pulse as an accumulation pulse.

When the stomach shows a large pulse, it indicates masses and accumulations. When the lungs have a faint pulse, accumulations gather under the right rib, the liver has accumulations, and qi accumulations appear — these concern the hand lung pulse.

Examining masses and accumulations: a large stomach pulse indicates a mass-accumulation; when the pulse is large and wiry-tight, it indicates accumulation in the vessels. A wiry pulse indicates accumulation; when the pulse is wiry, tight, and long with a deep hidden quality, it is an accumulation pulse.

Seeing the pulse of the stomach organ as large indicates a pass (guan position) wiry pulse. A single wiry-tight pulse corresponds to a condition below: easy to treat. A chi (cubit) position wiry-tight pulse that is faint and fine indicates kidney involvement.

Those who are weak and unable to generate strength will find the condition difficult to treat; if extremely deficient, death follows. The Jade Classic states: when the six pulse positions show abdominal accumulation, if the cun pulse is wiry and tight but the lower position is faint and fine, the kidney is involved.

When accumulations are present and the pulse is wiry and tight with both deep and floating qualities — the Five [Organs'] wiry accumulation pattern: the abdomen accumulates and gathers, the pulse is not hard or tight; wiry and fine with kidney involvement.

When the pulse is urgent, life is possible; when small and deficient, it indicates deficient excess with deep accumulation. When six positions show abdominal accumulation, the interior pulse is not hard and not tight — faint and fine, kidney involvement.

In the abdomen there is accumulation and masses: the pulse is deep, wiry, and hidden. The Jade Classic: whether yin, or deep-hidden, accumulation is present internally.

A wiry and urgent pulse means survival; a deficient and weak small pulse means death. The Jade Classic states: when the six positions show stomach accumulations gathering — if there is no strength, life is not possible; if deficient and weak and unable to survive, death follows.

Regarding painful masses and accumulations: the pulse is wiry at the front, fine, and deep; the heart generates a weak, deep, and floating pulse.

The weak, lingering stomach pulse: if it shows a heavy, sunken quality — there are also accumulation diseases with long duration; such pulses are mostly floating, high, wiry, and suddenly urgent.

In diagnosing women with accumulation and mass disorders: a wiry and urgent pulse indicates survival; a deficient, weak, and small pulse indicates death.

六鬱為積聚癥瘕疵瘤之本

不成。氣血沖和百病不生一有怫鬱諸病生焉。故氣血沖和而成癥此疾理也。又氣血不行血滯而成疾。因不得化仗血而為病也。血氣並而相因不得化仗失當也。此為不博化仗三日。此日氣化仗二。六濕鬱三日。此為六鬱二日。一日氣鬱當變而化不發得越此地大化當者帶而相因得之。降積成塊化不得者得化變而不成格越成疾疾帶而成。此而必成熱滿疾此必成熱疾結而成。

而滯濕不食鬱不消而成熱滿此而逢熱而成。

降衝不不得者不降當六鬱之病見先發。火風寒疾血一日。四鬱日之其變而化者。當鬱六鬱之法熟不順氣為風。

諸謂鬱解而總絡諸謂其降也。世析發也謂之分達多熱日積氣食少也此日六氣鬱化也二。此日為本達鬱分也。

喜謂也奪其解之金諸際世仲金之汪令其謂折之發今其謂源散之世解之吐令火內消日積達也和之火落發達之術蒸治也。

也謂土吐五利小便下也。今無鑢碎也謂之汗汪出之通之令謂之散也。

此世治解表利小便下也要耳水折之發令無鑢碎也。

九味葱麯和九。

方備下
translation:
The Six Stagnations are the Root of Accumulations, Gatherings, Concretions, Masses, Lumps, and Tumors

When qi and blood flow in harmony, the hundred diseases do not arise. Once there is constraint and stagnation, all manner of diseases are born. Therefore, when qi and blood flow in harmony, concretions form — this is the principle of disease. Moreover, when qi and blood fail to circulate, blood stagnates and disease forms. When it cannot be transformed, it relies on the blood to become disease. Qi and blood together mutually depend on one another; when transformation fails, the proper function is lost. This accounts for failure of transformation in three days. In the second day, qi transformation stagnates. In the third day of the six dampness stagnations. This is the second day of the six stagnations. On the first day, qi stagnation: what should change and transform does not disperse or escape; when it reaches a large accumulation, the stagnation bands together, one following the other. What descends and accumulates into lumps cannot transform; what can transform changes but fails to fully resolve, eventually forming disease. Disease accumulates and forms. This must become heat-fullness disease, and must then develop into knotted heat-disease.

Stagnant dampness, inability to eat, stagnation that does not disperse — this forms into heat-fullness, which then meets heat and solidifies.

What descends cannot descend, causing the six stagnations disease to first manifest. Fire, wind, cold, phlegm, and blood — on the first day. The four stagnations, after their changes and transformations, constitute the six stagnations method: turbid qi becomes wind.

All stagnation is said to resolve through the collaterals; reaching the depths of the stagnation, it dissipates. Dispersion through division achieves outward release of accumulated heat, distributing the qi and food to reduce them. This is the second day of the six qi stagnations transformation. This is the fundamental method of reaching and dispersing stagnation.

These methods — inducing vomiting, causing sweating, promoting urination, and purging downward — are the approaches for treating and resolving stagnation. Vomiting expels the earth; promoting urination and purging downward are used. Sweating disperses it outward; these are the general methods.

Treatment resolves the exterior, promotes urination, and purges downward. Water must be broken up and dispersed; sweating carries it out, and moving and dispersing methods are applied.

Nine-Ingredient Scallion and Medicated Leaven Harmony Pill.

translation:
Six Stagnations Decoction (六鬱湯)

Six Stagnations Decoction: A general treatment for all six types of stagnation. Ingredients: Cyperus rotundus (香附子) 2 qian; Ligusticum chuanxiong (川芎) and Atractylodes (蒼朮) 1 qian each; Pinellia ternata prepared (半夏製) and Massa medicata fermentata (神麴) stir-fried (炒) and Citrus peel (陳皮) 7 fen each; Red poria (赤茯苓) and Gardenia seed (梔子仁) 7 fen each; Forsythia (連翹) and Licorice (甘草) 5 fen each.

For qi stagnation, add Amomum villosum (縮砂) and Aucklardia root (木香). For blood stagnation, add Peach kernel (桃仁), Safflower (紅花), Tree peony bark (牡丹皮), and Chive juice (韭汁). For food stagnation, add Chinese hawthorn (山楂), Massa medicata (神麴), and White atractylodes (白朮). For dampness stagnation, add White atractylodes (白朮) and Poria (茯苓). For phlegm stagnation, add Trichosanthes (栝樓), Fritillaria (貝母), Arisaema (南星), and Pinellia (半夏). For heat stagnation, add Coptis (黃連), Gardenia (梔子), and Scutellaria (黃芩).

Six Stagnations Decoction variant: 5 fen to resolve all stagnations; decoct and take as tea. Ingredients include Cyperus (香附), Ligusticum (川芎), Atractylodes (蒼朮), Massa medicata stir-fried (神麴炒), Coptis (連), Fritillaria (貝母), Perilla leaf (紫蘇葉) 1 qian each, Citrus peel (陳皮), and Licorice (甘草).

Fermented Pill Formula (麴麴九)

Fermented Pill: Take 5 fen ginger to resolve all stagnations; grind into powder, form into pills with water the size of burdock seeds, take 7 pills with warm water.

Fermented Harmony-Preserving Pill (麴麴保和九)

Fermented Harmony-Preserving Pill: Opens stagnation, moves qi, disperses accumulation, and clears heat. Ingredients: Massa medicata stir-fried (神麴炒), White atractylodes (白朮), Cyperus (香附), Citrus peel (陳皮) 3 liang each; Chinese hawthorn (山楂) 2 liang; Atractylodes (蒼朮), Ligusticum (川芎), Massa medicata stir-fried.

For those whose illness does not resolve, it is appropriate to take this formula, including women, monks, and Taoist practitioners.

Each ingredient 5 fen; Licorice root (honey-fried) 3 fen. Cut the above into one dose.

Eight ingredients: Ligusticum chuanxiong, treats food [stagnation]; Ginger, Aged Tangerine Peel, Gardenia fruit, each 1 qian; Red Poria 2 fen; Decoct and take. Supplemented with each 1 qian; Half [a portion of] Atractylodes, White Peony Root.

Spontaneously resolves and generates [normal qi]. Epigastric region, apply Ginger 3 fen, decoct and take. Nourishes and supports pregnancy, in the middle, Yin.

Flatulence: spontaneously disperses and rises upward.

Section on the Classification of Abdominal Masses and Accumulations

Blood position: the diaphragm is the pathway of water and grain. Drink [retention] is in the middle; food accumulation is in the blood; accumulations and gatherings are in the middle, presenting as craving to drink. On the right it belongs to the Lung; drink retention is on the left; [masses] on the left belong to the Liver. The governing storage is then food and drink; left Guan [pulse] is the Liver; stomach is between.

Diagnosis and Treatment of Abdominal Masses

A mass is this type of abdominal condition. It is a tangible, transformable substance. It can form abdominal masses. It is caused by pathogenic factors and food accumulation wrapped in membranes internally; the skin and membranes wrap the accumulation externally. One should supplement substantially to treat it.

When the nine qi medicinals are unable to move [the mass], they work by moving the blood. Left position governs storage; then food and drink; left Guan is the Liver.

For the throat, it is appropriate to reduce [the mass] with Two-Aged Decoction (Er Chen Tang), adding food-dispersing and qi-supplementing, qi-moving medicinals to move [the accumulation]. This can remove the mass and then [restore] the thick [normal state].

When unable to move the person [i.e., the mass causes immobility], this is a blood-type abdominal mass. Or there may be formation, or there may be no mass; or blood [accumulation], named one type of abdominal mass; or below the viscera; or within the viscera.

[This page is from a classical Chinese medical text discussing treatments for abdominal masses and accumulations (塊/痞). The text describes several herbal formulas:]

Left or right side [masses]: if there is a hard lump (癰塊), both [sides] benefit from the formula. Soak in a hardening decoction; the pill is the main [treatment], each one [liang]. For flank masses:

Below, it is appropriate to take Danggui Longhui Wan (Angelica and Aloe Pill) to promote flow through the decoction and dissolve accumulations. For Baohe Kuai Wan (Preserve Harmony Mass Pill) and He Kuai Wan (Dissolve Mass Pill), add Chuan Shan Jia (pangolin scales), [take with] decoction.

[For masses], use Jiamei Cai Wan, Jupi Dan (Accumulation-Dispersing Elixir), which can combat [masses], both internally and externally; do not apply [paste] to the mass. It is appropriate to disperse [using] Chai Lian Ou Wan (Bupleurum-Coptis-Lotus Pill), four qian, add wood [ingredient], [in] pill form.

**Hua Kuai Wan (Mass-Dissolving Pill):**
Grind the following into powder: Hong Hua (safflower), vinegar-paste, Tao Ren (peach kernel), [plus] Wu Ling Zhi (flying squirrel feces), Hai Fen (cuttlefish powder), Xiang Fu (cyperus) soaked in vinegar, San Leng (sparganium) one liang, E Zhu (zedoary) five [qian] cooked in vinegar.

**Lian Luo Wan (Connecting-Network Pill):**
Bai Zhu (white atractylodes) ground into powder, mixed with vinegar paste into pills the size of wutong seeds, taken with warm water.

[Combined with] Xiang Fu (cyperus), stir-fried, remove seeds; [various ingredients] stir-fried, two liang, mixed with Zhi (bitter cardamom) to form the mass [pill]; for abdominal pain and borborygmus (intestinal rumbling), use Cang Bai Zhu (atractylodes).

Steam the cake with Ren He pills the size of tangerine seeds; take with plain warm water, [dosage] five to sixty pills, five qian.

translation:
Methods for Treating Accumulations and Gatherings (Ji Ju Zhi Fa)

When treating accumulations, one must examine their form and the associated pain to understand the nature of the disease — whether it is excess or deficiency — and thereby decide whether to drain or to supplement. One must carefully assess the location of the affected organs (high or low): what is high should be expelled upward; what needs supplementing should be drawn toward and guided.

What is bound should be treated with salty [purgatives]; what needs attacking should be dispersed; what is stagnant should be moved. Do not allow what has already been dispersed to linger. Use Ji (accumulation) pills to benefit the condition. Accumulations that are solid and gatherings that are mobile must be treated directly. Truly moving the condition requires regulating diet and being careful; otherwise simply using purgative medicines will only temporarily clear the accumulation. The root cause must be eliminated, for if only the manifestation is treated, the accumulation will merely return to its former place. One must harmonize the true qi; even external diseases can then be made to not worsen. Treat solid accumulations and moving gatherings with accumulation-dispelling pills to first strengthen [the patient], then use promoting pills.

Transforming medicines cause the disease to yield when diet is regulated carefully; otherwise downward-purging medicines alone will only temporarily clear the accumulation without removing its root. Do not use accumulation-dispelling [pills] lightly.

translation:
This page is from the Dongui Bogam (Encyclopedia of Eastern Medicine), discussing the classification and origins of various types of abdominal accumulations and masses (癰/癖/積/聚 — pathological lumps and accumulations in traditional East Asian medicine).

The text discusses:

Boils, carbuncles, and various named conditions including those caused by serpents (蛇), sharks (鮫), dragons (蛟龍), and birds (鶯), listing seven or eight categories of such afflictions, each with specific names.

It explains that accumulations (積, Ji) and gatherings (聚, Ju) arise from injury to food intake, blood stagnation, and pathological qi. When located in the abdomen or flanks, they may harden into fixed masses. There are those caused by blood stasis, those related to digestive dysfunction, and those arising spontaneously.

The text distinguishes between fixed accumulations (積), which have a definite location, and movable gatherings (聚), which disperse and reform. It discusses masses in the stomach and intestines, caused by food stagnation or blood pathology, and names conditions such as "gu" (蠱, parasitic disease), "pi" (痞, blockage), and "pi" (癖, habitual accumulation).

The passage concludes by noting these conditions are discussed in detail in the Maekmon (Pulse Gate) section, and that all these named diseases — whether from the seven or eight types of shark-named, dragon-fish-named, or snake-named categories — share underlying causes rooted in blood stagnation, qi accumulation, and dietary injury.

translation:
Intestinal Masses, Stone Conglomerations, and Blood-Gu: Diagnosis and Treatment

Take pills the size of a Chinese parasol seed, with a decoction of Chang Tang, seventy-nine pills per dose. Those with chronic accumulation diseases will be cured. When qi is stagnant in the heart, this formula should be tried to attack, supplement, or drain as appropriate, following ancient principles. Nourishing the correct qi will eliminate the condition.

Intestinal masses (chang tan) arise when cold qi lodges outside the intestines, contending with the stomach; the large intestine and surrounding flesh become knotted over time. As days pass, the large intestine and stomach contend together. The cold qi spreads, and after months the menstrual discharge ceases, or blood congeals into masses.

Stone conglomerations (shi jia): masses the size of eggs, with diminished qi, chronic illness resembling pregnancy. These intestinal masses should be pressed; they are hard. The approach is to push them away. After months the menses do not descend; blood conglomerates and becomes a mass.

In some cases the mass is egg-sized, qi is scant, and the illness is chronic like pregnancy. The intestinal blood mass when pressed is hard; it is appropriate to push it out. After months the menses do not descend, blood congeals into a mass. Old stone preparations and dispersing formulas promote passage, and the mass resolves.

For treatment, it is appropriate to use peach branch decoctions, then boil with blood-moving herbs, using san-leng (sparganium) to fortify the pill preparation.

When hard as stone, use peach kernel decoctions, then san-leng, fortifying the pill formula.

Cardamom (dry-fried), aged tangerine peel (dry-fried, white pith removed), prepared aconite, realgar (ground), one qian each. Grind to powder. Take with ginger decoction, twenty to thirty pills per dose.

Cardamom (dry-fried), tangerine peel (dry-fried, white pith removed), prepared aconite, croton seed — three qian each; prepared sand-fried peel, four qian, ground separately; croton — one part.

Form into pills the size of a Chinese parasol seed. Take with rice wine or ginger decoction, two qian per dose; with prepared pangolin scales.

Accumulation Disorder (Xi Ji Bing)

The Emperor asked: There are people who have illness with fullness below the ribs, with qi flowing in reverse — this persists for two or three years without resolving. What disease is this? Qi Bo replied: The disease is called Xi Ji (Breath Accumulation). This does not interfere with eating and cannot be treated by moxibustion or needling. It is appropriate to take the Mojeok-won (Accumulation-Grinding Pill) and Hwagi-tang (Qi-Transforming Decoction), along with Doin (Guiding) exercises.

Mojeok-won (Accumulation-Grinding Pill):
Treats accumulation of qi in the intestines and stomach, due to vacuity, settled outside the intestinal membrane and flowing to the ribs, having accumulated for many years and become difficult to treat — Breath Accumulation. Ten sprigs [of the herb]. Grind to powder; mix with rice and form into pills the size of mung beans. Take thirty pills per dose, swallowed with rice water.

Wood [ingredient], one part; Chaomu Xiang (aucklandia), two parts; Bai Jiang (patrinia), half part — grind to powder; form into pills with millet rice.

Hwagi-tang (Qi-Transforming Decoction):
Fennel (stir-fried), bitter orange shell (stir-fried), licorice — one wen each; [dosage] five characters [damaged]; grind to powder; cinnamon heart, costus root — two qian each; decoct with fresh ginger half [portion]; tangerine peel, green tangerine peel, clove skin — take as a beverage.

Doin (Guiding Exercise) Method:
Inhale again; send the breath downward; lie supine; at the appropriate time perform the exercise. Like this, thirty-six times, raise the qi — this is known as the fundamental node method; make fists and strike.

Pass through, repeatedly, stumbling breath; again begin with both hands; roll the accumulation [movement]; [various dosages]; grind to powder; cinnamon heart, costus root — two parts each; with fresh ginger [decoct]; twenty-one breath cycles; nurture the qi.

Purple perilla decoction: fry with radish, season with a little salt, herbs — one wen each.

Various Foods Causing Accumulation Disorders

When a person cannot properly digest due to weak stomach, or from excessive eating and drinking, or from excessive consumption of cold and raw foods:

The foods are not properly transformed and digested, leading to accumulation and gathering, forming lumps, with fullness and distension in the heart and abdomen.

Categories: (1) Pork, liver, lungs, fish, and crab accumulation, blood accumulation; (2) Fruit and vegetable accumulation; (3) Wine/alcohol accumulation (13 days); (4) Tea accumulation (8 days).

Food Accumulation:
Use Bowel-Protecting Spirit Pill to aid digestion; for accumulation, use Calm Stomach Powder, adding Fructus Amomi (Suo Sha) and fragrant herbs. Food accumulation is suitable for treatment with Zuo Jiu Lian, fresh ginger, and perilla, decocted and taken. Add Fructus Amomi. For lodged food accumulation, use ginger, perilla decoction. For food accumulation, use red poria and raphanus pills taken continuously.

Alcohol Accumulation:
For those who drink excessively and develop accumulation, use red poria and raphanus pills continuously.

Use mung beans, yellow, fire-processed, ground fine, combined with Shen Qu (medicated leaven), prepared with water; use Xian Dan (Immortal Elixir) and the toad formula, with aromatic meats, wine, finely ground, taken to disperse accumulation, combined with honey-prepared water, taken in doses.

Flour/Noodle Accumulation:
For those who eat too much rice and grain, develop accumulation with sour sensation in the heart and abdomen, take Qingmu (Aucklandia) decoction; if ineffective, take Xian Dan Toad Formula. Also use Gui Bao Hua Jie, aromatic meats prepared in wine, taken regularly as pills; this also treats alcohol accumulation. Use pueraria wine decoction.

Grind finely, combine with honey-prepared water, take in doses with medicated leaven; use concentrated decoction with wine to send down, using one qian, concentrated in paper, taken as a drink.

Page 32 of Dongui Bogam, Tangaekpyeon (Herbal Remedies Section), containing three prescriptions:

**Amwi-gu (Asafoetida Pill)**
Take two liang of yellow [ingredient], grind to powder, stir-fry with salt, mix with fermented wheat cakes and noodles, add tangerine peel, dried citrus peel, adzuki beans, aged tangerine peel; take with vinegar paste formed into pills. **Samnŭng Jeon-won (Three-Edge Bulrush Decoction Pill)**
Treats internal injury with abdominal swelling and pain. Scrape the [ingredient] to fine powder, eight liang, mix with three sheng of vinegar and three sheng of stone, stir-fry the radish and three-edge bulrush together, stir-fry green [ingredients], combine into a paste.

**Myoŭng-dan (Wondrous Response Elixir)**
Ingredients: various components each three liang, half a liang of tangerine peel, seven qian, wheat-processed [ingredient], remove bran, do not use; mix with tangerine peel, make into portions; eat with water; dissolve hard masses and accumulations; break up stagnation; treat worm accumulations, food stagnation, or box-shaped masses; mixed with vinegar and attached [herbs], four liang each, seven doses.

Treats abdominal food stagnation, fish-bone lodgment, worm accumulations, hard masses; sun-dry, remove skin, treat internal injury.

translation:
Cinnamon Fragrance Pill (Guixiang Wan)
Treats overeating of mixed fruits leading to food accumulation, abdominal distension, and urgent qi (gas). Cinnamon heart: 1 liang.

Moji Yuan (Accumulation-Grinding Pill)
Treats meat accumulation and reduced food intake, sallow complexion, abdominal pain. Old granary rice: half sheng; Croton seed (Badou): added; Green tangerine peel and tangerine red: 2 liang each; simmer in mild ginger decoction; good vinegar-fried; combined with red beans, remove skin; cimicifuga (shengma). Grind to powder: vinegar, dried tangerine peel, dried ginger; pills about the size of a seed; with good ginger, stir-fry qi accumulation; equal parts: sparganium (sanleng), atractylodes (zhu), cyperus (xiangfu).

Shenghong Yuan (Victorious Red Pill)
Take with vinegar, large stir-fried blood decoction. For the above: dried tangerine peel, dried ginger; pills of good ginger; accumulation qi, stir-fry; equal parts: 1 liang each; sparganium, atractylodes, cyperus. Decoct with Four Substances Decoction adding sparganium and atractylodes.

Augmented Four Substances Decoction (Zengwei Siwu Tang)
Treats phlegm-blood accumulation. Take standard Four Substances Decoction formula, add three portions of sparganium and atractylodes.

Sparganium Decoction (Sanleng Jian Tang)
One method: dry-roast over fire, eat with 1 liang; [for] urinary obstruction with wine, crush for blood accumulation, abdominal qi; standard decoction formula, three portions, add sparganium, processed herb; 4 liang each [various ingredients].
Roast sparganium, take atractylodes, 2 liang each; green tangerine peel, magnolia flower bud (xinyi), atractylodes, stir-fry; 5 pills each lightly scorched; combine all.
Grind to powder; vinegar 6 sheng, same with atractylodes 3 liang; add green tangerine flower; add vinegar in decoction, stir-fry; fill cup without [opening], lightly seal the mouth.

Grind to powder. Preparation method and administration method same as above.

Ingredients: Muxiang (costus root), Binlang (areca nut), Chenpi (tangerine peel), Qingpi (green tangerine peel), Zhike (bitter orange), Ezhu (zedoary) — each 5 qian; Bai Chou (white morning glory seed) head powder 6 qian; Shenqu (medicated leaven), Maiya (barley sprout) — 3 qian each; Badou (croton seed). General Medicines for Treating Accumulations, Lumps, Phlegm, and Masses

Sanleng (burr reed rhizome), Ezhu — for dispersing accumulations; Jiuzhong Wan for relaxing the middle; Wanbao Yuan; take with Wenbai Yuan, Wanbing Yuan, Huajin Lu Wan; Yaojian Yuan; secret formula.

[Treats] ten types of wind, ten types of water qi, eight types of pi (stuffiness), seven types of zheng (abdominal masses), twelve types of jaundice, heart pain, distant abscesses, ten types of water qi, eight types of ailments, seven types of zheng, twelve types of cold.

Ingredients include: roasted Wutou (aconite main root) 2 liang, roasted Fuzi (aconite), Wuzhuyu (evodia), Jiegeng (platycodon), Chaihu (bupleurum), Ziwan (aster), dried [ginger], Chuanjiao (Sichuan pepper), and other connecting dried Chuan [herbs].

[Various other ingredients and preparations follow for treating abdominal accumulations, masses, and various illnesses.]

[The pill] treats long-standing illness and weakness, various chronic diseases. Honey pills the size of a large jujube, taken with ginger decoction... treats women's conditions [as well].

Jingpong Jeoneo (Schizonepeta-Typhonium Decoction Pill)

Treats cold and heat accumulations, masses, conglomerations, various abdominal lumps, and aids digestion of food stagnation. Uses Sanleng (Sparganium).

The ingredients are ground into powder. Twelve to twenty-eight liang. Cyperus, costus root, processed with wine for three days, stir-fried until yellow, then for one day stir-fried together with croton seed, soaked [in liquid].

Large ginger powder, taken with decoction. Changes jade pieces, cut nineteen leaves, cardamom seed, same day, one decoction soak.

Secret Formula Huazhi Pill (Stagnation-Dissolving Pill)

Its function is to regulate yin and yang, resolve all types of accumulation and retention, dissolve masses, remove old hard lumps, treat deep-seated accumulations, abrasive and unblocking, eliminating cold blockage.

Grind to fine powder. Pinellia. On the right: costus root, clove, fragrant ingredients cut, remove old accumulated lumps, melting deep stagnation, unblocking.

Twenty-nine portions each: crow's-end powder, tangerine peel, green tangerine peel, medicated food, coptis root, white [atractylodes], rhubarb, four qian each.

Decoction taken. Lotus powder, eight, white, six, skin, medicated leek, remove, white, coptis, four qian each.

If accumulation is large, each dose uses two portions with decoction, up to eighteen portions, dry medicated leek, remove, white, coptis, four qian each.

If little accumulation, use mume fruit flesh, dried, each several qian.

Sanleng Huaji Pill (Sparganium Accumulation-Dissolving Pill)

Take with decoction. Each dose, stop at six portions, if wishing to promote bowel movement, boil in water until cooked.

For severe stagnation, each dose with yellow wine, steam accumulation, three decoctions, up to nineteen portions, white, six, peel, medicated leek, remove each.

For accumulation, each dose uses two with decoction, up to eighteen portions, dry medicated leek, remove.

Guide each to stop at six, if wishing to promote movement, use small amount of meat flesh, boiled until cooked.

Ligusticum, stir-fried, Arisaema, tangerine peel, aconite, magnolia bark, processed with wine, steamed accumulation, three decoctions, stop at nine portions, white, six, peel, medicated leek removed.

Peach kernel, dried, stir-fried, pounded, white atractylodes, decoction, one, four liang, fifty-nine portions, powder, vinegar.

Paste, mixed, stir-fried, inserted, white atractylodes, decoction, four or five, fifty-nine portions, powder, vinegar.

Coptis root, stir-fried, amomum, medicated leek, stir-fried yellow.

translation:
Patch Plaster for Masses (貼痞膏)

Ingredients: Iron filings, fruit (likely hawthorn), red to the degree of bone color, silk thread, water, fermented liquid, safflower, child-fist-sized pieces, 2 qian of realgar, lard, mirabilite (sodium sulfate), shan bi (mountain loquat), moxa — each 1 qian.

Method: Use ingredients in proportion to bone-colored fruit. After combining, add meat the size of a chicken egg, pound together into a paste (膏). Use one bottle of wine to apply and stimulate. After three days the cloth covering is removed.

Method for Suppressing Accumulations (厭厭法):

Apply vermilion, myrrh, and other ingredients; stir-fry black until like ink powder. Then use wine mixed and boiled, apply as a hot compress. Wrap in cloth to induce sweating.

Gripping Medicine to Declare Accumulations (握藥宣積):

Wash hands at the time of use. Fill the hand and wish to stop. The old cough and wheezing, the rushing pulse — treat from where it originates. When the accumulation is small and difficult to treat, it must be addressed urgently or death will result. The five accumulations, including Running Piglet (奔豚) syndrome in the center.

Difficult-to-Treat Conditions (難治證):

When the patient dies with rushing pulse returning, and the surging pulse is at its most vigorous, with coughing and wheezing from the rushing and turning pulse — if one gets the small and difficult-to-treat pulse, death is near.

Discussion: Wang Shan's theory holds that these diseases arise from calling out in distress and mental confusion. This refers to the condition of the patient. Nourishing the tiger only invites its attack — prolonged tonification of long-standing accumulations only worsens them. These are difficult conditions for a person not to fear.

Simple Formulas, 9 types, 2

Achyranthes Root (Niuxi): 4 varieties
For sudden abdominal pain with a feeling like stones pressing inside, with fine bitter herbs, take [decoction] each morning, take for three to seven days, warming and serving on an empty stomach, twice [daily] — effective.

Corydalis (Yuanhu Suo):
For breaking up accumulations and masses, grinding into powder, cooking with vinegar into a paste, forming pills the size of a paulownia seed — effective for large accumulations and stagnation. Add fresh ginger, decoct nineteen times in vinegar, cook into a paste pills — effective for masses, old and new, promoting circulation over one hundred days, otherwise death may result.

Rhubarb (Dahuang):
For heat accumulations and gatherings, removing skin rashes. Grind five liang into a fine powder, with honey make pills, decocting with fresh ginger — eliminates old conditions and brings on the new, resolves within one hundred days, otherwise one will die. If abdominal pain feels like stabbing and there is no relief, many die.

Phytolacca Root (Shanglü):
Primarily treats sudden abdominal fullness. Take the root of phytolacca alone, steam it, then wrap it with cloth on the abdomen. [If there are hidden masses] inside like stones causing stabbing pain and discomfort, this brings relief and recovery — easy treatment.

Morning Glory Seed (Qianniu Zi):
Stir-fry, make into honey pills for accumulations and gatherings, abdominal masses and fullness. Extremely effective for abdominal distension like stones, pain so severe one wishes to die. Use black morning glory seeds, take the top portion, powder half, with kudzu vine root, small fresh ginger — marvelously effective in three days.

Agastache/Patchouli (Huoxiang):
Finely slice and stir-fry, use with wine. For sudden abdominal hardness like stone with stabbing pain, abdominal distension lasting three nights — take five doses daily for three days, divine effect.

It is prescribed for all manner of accumulations and stagnation. Taking it regularly will stop diarrhea immediately.

桑耳 (Mulberry ear fungus)
Burned to ash, it is indicated for blood disorders, abdominal masses, and hidden accumulations. Take the root decocted and drink.

虎杖根 (Japanese knotweed root)
Indicated for hidden abdominal masses with pain. Soak in wine and take mixed with the powder. One day combined:
For festering sores, flatulence, and masses such as hidden beam accumulation and fish-turtle type masses, roast until yellow with garlic.

translation:
Causes of Edema

Edema

Moxibustion with as many cones as one's age is applied to sores, carbuncles, abscesses, swellings on the feet and ankles, and lumps within sores; this will spontaneously cure them. Salt is placed [on the site] and moxibustion is applied above it.

For conditions such as Running Piglet disorder and deep-seated pulse, and for accumulations and gatherings (積聚), take Zhongwan (中脘); for Zhangmen (章門), Guanmen (關門), and Qihai (期中); for intestinal accumulation and lumps, take Zhangmen (章門) and Guanmen (關門) during the middle period.

At the abdominal cavity and qi points, at Tianshu (天樞), take Shangwan (上脘) and Lianggu (梁谷), opening through Sanguia and Shanmen. Specifically treating lumps on the left side: moxibustion is applied both left and right, going down the left side to the foot, measuring to the tip of the large toe.

The point location is on the left side behind the abdomen; moxa is applied at the center. The method uses a measure of half a cun; apply moxa to the afflicted area, measuring from the patient's left side down to the foot, reaching the tip of the large toe.

Going from Bangshuang (傍壯) point, opening with Shengui (神跟), double moxa, non-dispersing method; then on the left foot behind the second toe, on the right side moxa is applied at the tailbone, measuring the patient from foot to the tip of the large toe.

By evening the patient will feel rumbling in the abdomen — this is the sign that moxibustion is working. Behind the gate (門), one or two finger-widths, on the right side apply moxa at the tailbone, measuring from the patient's foot.

For wheezing, the spleen, the middle burner, the pulse, water metabolism, the lower burner — when the spleen is edematous due to cold-heat, qi and yin in the lungs become bound, then qi transformation fails and water accumulates, resulting in fullness with yin binding.

translation:
Subtle Signs of Edema (Swelling)

It is asked: why does the Lesser Yin govern water? The answer: The kidney is a yin organ, residing at the deepest level of yin. The lung serves as the canopy of the kidney. The kidney belongs to Lesser Yin. Why does it govern water?

Answer: The kidney is the organ of water. It gathers water and follows its root. The root is in the kidney, which generates disease. The kidney's winter pulse reaches the deepest yin, gathers water and follows its origin in the generation of disease. This relates to the skin and flesh, hence the closure of passages.

When swelling occurs due to deficiency, the lower passages are not free, so water accumulates and disease arises. Water overflows downward; the lower burner fails to filter the fluids. The yang pathways become blocked; the skin and flesh all swell, which is called skin swelling.

When abdominal distension occurs, water is gathered and disease arises. Water flows downward; the lower burner does not filter the liquid. The qi pathways are obstructed throughout. Water overflows into the four limbs and the skin.

The face and eyes become puffy and distended. The abdomen distends like a drum. The face and eyes swell. This is due to the bladder; the skin becomes like a great drum, with the face and eyes swollen.

This is called water swelling disease, also known as kidney transmission disease. It is also called kidney accumulation or drum distension — all of these arise from the kidney organ and bladder being deficient and swollen.

The condition arises from the intestines and stomach. Water and grain accumulate, flowing through the body. When the waterways and fluid passages are obstructed, water overflows and swells throughout the body, the face, and the four limbs.

Water accumulates in the intestines and remains in the lower burner. The fluids cannot be filtered, and they flow along the sides of the intestines.

The waist region: this condition is also called heavy kidney accumulation, kidney adhesion, and drum distension. The kidney is also called the governing transmitter.

When the waist becomes heavy and movement is difficult, the bladder fills with heat. The face and abdomen swell. The liver, heart, spleen, lung, and kidney all transmit disease to the stomach, bladder, and intestines.

As for all the general signs — edema of the limbs, herbal treatments, water swelling with visible fullness — the lower abdomen and waist are also affected.

Signs and Symptoms of Edema (Fushong/Bujonghyeongjeung)

Regarding yin-type edema: it resembles lying down with a fragrant rising sensation; the wood element affects the abdomen, causing water accumulation that must be expelled through urination. The head and neck region shows vascular swelling with movement. This is an internal illness.

When water accumulates in the fragrant and new rising areas, the legs and shins become swollen. The skin of the neck becomes swollen and pulsates, causing difficulty swallowing and pressing sensations. The hands and feet become numb above.

When unable to move the large joints freely, the body becomes inflamed internally and fluids and essence seep downward, causing fluid to flow and drain from the shin region. This black condition involves water accumulation that suppresses the appetite.

The disease involves water accumulating below; the lung vessels become distended with the abdomen enlarged, and fluids seep internally so that fluid drains downward dispersing, but food and drink cannot be taken.

The kidney governs water swelling; the lung governs the upper region. When breathing becomes labored and water cannot pass through, one cannot recover.

When the bone joints are swollen and painful with delayed pulse, there is wind-type skin disease involved.

The three types of swelling: the first type involves water accumulation where pressing reveals sinking; the pulse is slow and sluggish due to wind.

Five categories of edema type:
The second type resembles wearing a basin over the abdomen — the skin cannot develop sweating externally, and when swelling closes off water becomes trapped.

The fifth sign involves panting and sweating. The fourth type is stone-water edema with a slow pulse; the body's muscles become saturated with fullness in all four limbs and the abdomen, with swelling. Moxibustion is applied.

There are also five organ water conditions: Heart-water — the body is heavy with little energy, unable to lie down, restless and agitated, the abdomen enlarged.

translation:
This page from the Dongui Bogam discusses various types of edema (水腫, water swelling) and related conditions. The text describes the following clinical presentations and their characteristics:

Lying on one's side with irritability, great swelling of the genitals, fluids not passing smoothly, difficulty with urination, but occasional loose watery stools like duck droppings. When water accumulates, the abdomen becomes large and the patient cannot turn over. The abdomen is greatly distended; it is difficult to urinate in small amounts. There is a sensation of qi rising with dampness, difficulty urinating, and a cry-like sound. The skin over the abdomen is thin, the yang qi and yin water extend to the hands, feet, and body, and the abdomen is distended. Internally, the yin water fills the abdomen and waist; the patient wants to sleep. There is also yellowing and thinning of the skin. The eyes, gallbladder, and lower regions are damp. The intestines and stomach have floating sensations. The abdomen is full and weak with reduced gallbladder function. Suffering is great. The legs and feet are numb. Water exposure, getting caught in rain, wind-cold, or summer heat and dampness affect the waist. Internally, the hands and arms, the back, exposure to water and summer heat, wind-cold cause difficulty with urination, fatigue, great thirst, and constipation. The kidneys are enlarged; urination stops and becomes scant, urine is not reddish, the lower body is swollen, the abdomen and waist are bound and the legs are hard.

Yang type edema: the same difficulty with urination, kidney enlargement, urine stoppage, scant and not reddish urine, lower body swelling, abdominal binding.

Soaking in cold water, drinking cold tea and alcohol, exposure of the arms and back to water, getting caught in rain or summer heat, wind-cold: these cause reddish or scanty urine, difficulty sleeping, lower body swelling, constipation, and hardness of the legs.

Upper yang type: the body is swollen externally, the arms and back are exposed to water and rain, wind-cold and summer dampness affect the waist.

Floating edema becoming full edema, jaundice, vomiting, dysentery, numbness of the hands and feet. Immediately the abdomen becomes full and distended.

Cold type: large abdomen with accumulated fluids, swelling of the waist, pain and swelling. The suffering is unbearable.

Severe cases: heaviness of the body, abdominal fluid accumulation, difficulty with urination, constant discomfort.

In the morning, internally the abdomen is hard as stone. Gradually the abdomen distends fully with water. The patient craves water, the skin wastes away, there is morning urgency, blood deficiency, qi deterioration, tearing of the abdomen. Water accumulates and the skin becomes toxic, the body develops abscesses and pus collects, hardening in the lower regions.

translation:
Pulse Method

When the pulse is deep (sunken) and fine, the condition is treatable. If the body is swollen and heavy, the abdomen greatly enlarged — in water disease, a pulse that is surging and large indicates death and is difficult to treat. In water swelling, the pulse is necessarily deep; when the water qi subsides, the condition improves but tends to recur. In yin-type water swelling, the pulse is mostly deep and rapid. In yang-type water disease, the pulse is floating. When there is upward qi with floating swelling and the pulse is sunken, the condition is difficult to treat.

Treatment Methods for Water Swelling (Edema)

Use [herbs] to regulate the qi and control floating swelling. For lower lung conditions, it is appropriate to add Magnolia bark (houpu) and tangerine peel to tonify the center and disperse abdominal qi and dampness. The fundamental treatment uses Atractylodes (cangzhu) as the chief herb, using yang to promote urination. Add winter ingredients and aromatics in the form of a white [decoction].

To promote sweating and transform [the pathogen], consolidate the fu-organs, direct fluid flow toward urination, and thus easily drain moisture — enter into the abdominal swelling through the gateway of water.

When the disease transforms water qi and permeates the fu-organs, use [herbs] to direct flow, promote urination, and disperse [the accumulation], treating the swelling and addressing the blood aspect.

The lung governs the descent of qi. The method should clear and open the pathways, allowing turbid qi to be expelled while pure qi is retained. Use cold [natured herbs] to restrain [excess], guide kidney qi, promote urination, and eliminate [the pathogen].

When the pulse is vacuous and floating, the condition is treatable. When it is sunken and rough or large, one should aim for it to become fine. Water disease with a sunken and fine pulse is favorable. When water generates qi vacuity and the pulse is floating, death is indicated; a large pulse indicates difficulty in treatment and one should aim for fineness. Compare yin pulses. When there is upward qi with floating swelling and a sunken pulse, [the prognosis is poor].

Page 49 of Dongui Bogam, Herbal Medicine Volume 1. The page contains four herbal remedy formulas:

Taeksa-san (澤瀉散 — Alisma Powder):
Take three fen. Treats water swelling. Two portions: promotes urination. Grind the following to powder: Alisma (Taeksa), Ox knee (牛頭), equal portions of Red Poria (赤茯苓), and Ophiopogon (石). Grind to powder. Ginger, Coix, White Atractylodes.

Shinho-san (神助散 — Spirit-Assisting Powder):
Eight doses. Use a mirror-polished stone. Take one sheng of water, simmer with three portions of white [herb], add five cups' worth. Combine and heat several times, until it passes ten li of the way through the body. Each dose: three qian each of various herbs including Ze-mu (Alisma wood), aromatics (香), three qian each. Treats water swelling, clears the eyes, relieves edema, promotes urination. Filters black liquid. Three years of chronic [condition] relieved, used for long-standing illness.

Mahuang Gancao Tang (麻黃甘草湯 — Ephedra and Licorice Decoction):
Use four sheng of water. Boil and reduce. Take one dose per day, apply one plaster on top of the floating swelling. Relieves accumulated and long-standing swelling that does not improve. Warm the preparation. Licorice two qian. Induce mild sweating. Take again. Right side: cut and prepare.

Yuepei Tang (越脾湯 — Spleen-Overcoming Decoction):
Treats upper-body sweating swelling, cough, and wheezing. Huang (Astragalus) three qian, Cang-zhu (Atractylodes) two qian. Taken with water. Licorice each one qian. Cut and prepare as one packet. Add ginger five slices, jujube two pieces.

translation:
Huangmi Pill (Yellow Millet Pill)
Treats water [retention/edema]. Take millet grains, four doses, steam together with dried silk gourd, stir-fry with beans, remove skin, cut into pieces, mix with croton seeds, add to aged meat. Add to collaterals, draw with silk skin, also use beans each time, decoct, reduce the amount, stir-fry together, take one hundred pills, serve with rice water immediately to heal, and benefit the collaterals, take the gourd, add to water.

Lacquer and Realgar Pill
Mix with mutton and Firmiana seeds, decoct, swallow large doses, take four doses below the sea gate [navel area]. Dry realgar, one liang, one liang, melt inside a pot, grind into powder, squeeze through hemp cloth to remove dregs. Add back to water, cook with salt, inside truly raw damp, cut all water, open and dissolve the floating [edema].

Sanhua Shenyou Pill (Three Flowers Divine Protection Pill)
Treats edema due to deficiency, pathogenic water fullness, flowing into the waist and knees causing floating swelling and pain. Gansui (Euphorbia kansui), raw jade [Prepared components]. Accumulation of swelling in various areas, opening dampness and floating. Use huangdi water paper, four portions forming residue, seeds, one qian, stored abdominal pain, gansui, raw jade.

Warm Kidney Pill
Open [the channels], remove fascia, process wood, clove fragrance, one liang, grind into powder, send down with mint decoction. For external use, use huangdi water as residue. Heavy membrane, roast over fire, medicine taken at bedtime, chew finely inside the mouth, send down with mint leaf decoction, externally remove, use huangdi water paper, four portions as residue.

Five Peels Powder
When other diseases transform into water swelling and edema. One qian each of Dafupi (Areca peel) and Poria peel, cut and combine into one packet, decoct in water.

translation:
Edema located in the bladder: use택사(Alisma) as the root remedy. The eighth type is called "high water," which first causes swelling beginning from the lower abdomen; the root remedy is soybean. The ninth type uses red adzuki bean. For the tenth type, among the nine kinds of water qi, use red adzuki bean, or for the root source, remove one ingredient and double another.

Ten Water Pills (十水丸)
This formula treats the lord of more than ten types of water qi using red adzuki bean, or for the root source, remove one ingredient and double another. Prepared from refined powder made into honey pills. Dietary restrictions apply. Take with food. One hundred pills, taken three times daily for twenty-one days.

Jieyang Syndrome (結陽證)
When qi is deficient in the four limbs and becomes scattered, causing heat and accumulation — this is called Jieyang (Bound Yang). The four limbs become swollen with pathogenic qi. According to the Suwen (Plain Questions), when exuberant correct qi encounters dampness-heat with added yang, the correct qi is unable to circulate freely, and therefore swelling and pain develop at all four extremities. The treatment is to disperse and regulate.

Rhinoceros Horn Decoction (犀角湯)
This decoction mainly treats Jieyang syndrome, with swelling of the four limbs and swelling and pain of the joints. Ingredients: rhinoceros horn, scrophularia root (玄參) — 1 qian each; cimicifuga (升麻), licorice (甘草).

Divide into portions of 5 fen each, make one packet, decoct in water and take; in winter add bupleurum (柴胡) — 4 fen each; aquilaria (沉香), belamcanda (射干), licorice (甘草) — 6 fen each.

Classification of Qi-aspect and Blood-aspect Disorders

Qi-aspect: When the pulse shows redness and swelling, it is appropriate to use a decoction. Blood-aspect: This is also called "water-aspect." Guizhi-Fuling Decoction addresses swelling caused by obstruction. [Use with] paste. Pungent [herbs], Licorice, equal parts.

Guizhu Decoction: Treats excess in the qi-aspect. [Ingredients:] Dried ginger, various herbs, seven and a half fen each. Right side: Atractylodes, Ephedra, finely sliced, made into one packet, with ginger, five pieces.

[Another formula]: Treats excess in the pattern [of accumulation]. [Ingredients:] Bitter orange, Magnolia bark, Cinnamon bark, White Atractylodes, Red Poria, Thunder-processed Angelica, Ligusticum, Red Peony, Green tangerine peel, Water chestnut herb, Aged Atractylodes. Take with water decoction.

Guifu Decoction: Treats interior water-aspect condition. [Ingredients:] White skin, Red Poria, Atractylodes, Large Arecae peel, Ligusticum skin, Piper longum, each equal parts; Large Arecae peel, with ginger and jujube, decocted in water, take two cups with half [spoon of] salt.

Formulas for edema before and after childbirth in women: All found in the Extraordinary Techniques Hall.

[Method to] eliminate water without taking medicine:

Chamber Extraordinary Technique: Treats swelling and bloating of the umbilical region that does not resolve. Separately take medicine to expel the water. Grind Croton seed, remove the oil, grind into a cake the size of a coin.

[Pill formula:] Use fresh cotton cloth, one piece; Calomel, two qian; Sulfur; Cover with raw [herb], [apply coins outside], bind with five吊, attach the cake, wait for water to descend, after three to five [times], blow away the medicine.

One Formula: For treatment, add white kidney [ingredients], one cup of akebia wood (Mutong), purple leaf vegetable decoction, Clear-Flow Decoction below, then take aquilaria qi-moving drink as a topical application.

Another Formula: Stomach membrane powder — after gastric [condition], forms an abscess. Grind to powder or set in water bubble, apply wet; when abscess forms, dry and apply earth-clay, which will immediately break down the mass and level it.

Signs of Treatable versus Untreatable Conditions: If [urine fills] a full bowl, soft scrotal swelling is treatable. The patient has generalized swelling; good prognosis for swelling. Men with swelling starting from the feet upward, women with chronic retention [of fluid] retreating upward from the thighs — [prognosis noted accordingly].

Black Soybeans
For treating a hoarse throat, grind into powder and take on an empty stomach with alcohol. Tokbi (冬介/善介薢 — a plant remedy)
For those newly afflicted with disease, this remedy is effective. Or in urgent cases, take the juice. For long-standing illness, there is no limit — take it for seven days. Chicken Urine
For treating [edema/swelling]: use alcohol and water; when the swelling begins to stir and rumble internally, coming out through the large intestine, the illness disperses. 帝曰脹者亦生何因而有岐伯曰陽氣相在順衛氣之逆陰陽相攻勢五臟六腑皆行有遇伯日衛氣之逆陰陽相攻外郁內蒸為脈遲時上有所傷其脈氣相攻伐六脈脹兩化氣外侵欲歌食脈

脹滿之源

乃得乃在天榮地氣止寒始脈氣迻時上有所傷真所為五相攻伐六脈脹兩化氣外侵欲歌食脈

失水前分為募腧之七情氣內遷傷為六脈脹兩化氣外侵欲歌食脈不能致運濕鬱化脾之土陰升發陰陽之氣輸之之成滿淪血膀經謝

translation:
Acupuncture and Moxibustion Methods

Regarding acupuncture and moxibustion: On the four limbs and face, where swelling is present, moxibustion at Shuifen (Water Division) and Qihai (Sea of Qi) points leads to death. For people with water swelling, only moxibustion should be used; needling at Shuifen is the most dangerous and deadly point, as this area relates to the Sea point, and many people with water swelling have died from it.

Abdominal Distension and Fullness

The Emperor asked: "Distension — how does it arise and from what cause?" Qi Bo replied: "When Yang qi encounters reversal, Wei (defensive) qi moves in reverse, Yin and Yang clash against each other, all five zang organs and six fu organs are affected. The Wei qi reverses, Yin and Yang attack each other, causing internal and external stagnation, creating slow pulse, and where there is injury above, the pulse qi attacks internally causing the six pulses to become distended, transforming qi outward."

The Origin of Abdominal Distension and Fullness

When the Ying (nutritive) and Wei (defensive) qi are formed from Heaven's nourishing and Earth's qi, the pulse qi moves in time; where there is damage, the true force of the five interactions attacks the six pulse channels, causing distension and transforming outward qi stagnation.

When the seven emotions disturb qi internally, this injures the six pulse channels and causes distension, transforming and driving qi outward.

When the ascending and descending movement of Yin and Yang qi is disrupted, dampness accumulates and the spleen-earth fails to transform, leading to fullness, blood stasis, and obstruction of the channels.

This condition called "Drum Distension" arises when pathogenic heat lodges and over time transforms through qi, with dampness accumulating and stagnating, the condition being likened to a drum. The disease affects the bladder and channels and is difficult to treat, hence it is also called "Gu" (parasitic drum). The pattern of drum distension arises when heat lodges, qi transformation fails, dampness stagnates, and the middle transforms into this condition of drum-like abdominal distension.

text:
脹滿形證

之義。飲食不節起居不時。陰受之。陰氣壅而不散。則成脹。氣謂太陰寒氣在腹。陽明之脈病足太陰之脈。亦聚在上則成膜脹。日足太陰氣謂腹脹。則生膜脹。腹不能大。乃至太陰乃為滿脹。五水壅腫。几九滿膜脹肥。初起故是膜脹中。欲食則胃陰明經之云太。

音樂不治。其面目四肢腹脹也。即膜四肢腫者者。盈而不治。更難也。謂水壅腫。三玉行年而後。飲食如常消成補腫稍進益補中。導治更腫薄鹽膂食中。

效乃安。中滿腹脹。不可盡以眠。速必瘡。補三玉行濕無以成消。導治常腫推補益補中鹽膂食中。

行不減及足常。成水寒治比水深更。五陰太大乃至。亦寒所謂乃為富寒飲女。故陽中欲乂則胃陰。

則生膜脹腹。不能大。陽膜不蠕能。○○足濁太氣謂腹脹。則成膜脹氣病。腹寒在足陽明之脈病。不散。則成膜脹。

寶投之。則胸膈而有軟膜虛實。脹膜為熱鄭。利不熟食時乾膜。當時減滿內納腹之痛者為。故此為寒虛宜溫痛之者為。按之不痛為故此。寒虛宜溫痛之。腹硬門時減滿。復按如故此不為寒虛宜溫。之者為○。水脹膜中但膜空四肢脹下。甚腫也。臨冒為盡。在足太陰也。轉明腹轉明腹者壅起。

translation:
Forms and Symptoms of Abdominal Distension (Zhangman Xingzheng)

The meaning is this: When diet and eating are without restraint, and daily life and rest are without regularity, the yin receives the harm. The yin qi becomes congested and does not disperse, thus forming distension. This refers to the cold qi of the Taiyin lodging in the abdomen. The Yangming channel and the Taiyin channel are diseased; qi also gathers above and thus forms membranous distension. It is said: when the Taiyin qi causes abdominal distension, membranous distension arises. The abdomen cannot enlarge greatly; eventually it reaches the Taiyin stage and becomes full distension. The five types of water congestion cause swelling. When membranous distension first arises, if one still desires food, it is the stomach and Yangming channel issue.

When music and pleasure do not help, the face, eyes, four limbs, and abdomen become distended. That is, membranous swelling of the four limbs and abdomen occurs. Being full yet untreated, it becomes even harder to cure. This is called water congestion swelling. After several years, eating and drinking may seem normal, but the swelling gradually diminishes only with supplementation — one must guide the treatment, strengthen the center, and use supplementing foods with moderate saltiness.

Only then will there be relief. For central fullness and abdominal distension, one cannot simply rely on rest. It will quickly lead to sores. Supplementation and guiding the dampness out is the approach; otherwise it will not resolve.

When the flow is reduced and the feet feel cold, water-cold treatment is compared. The Taiyin and greater yin reach extreme states, and the cold is so-called causing swelling of the abdomen with cold and dryness.

Membranous distension arises; the abdomen cannot enlarge greatly; the membrane of the yang cannot move freely. The Taiyin qi is said to cause abdominal distension, thus forming membranous distension and qi disease; abdominal cold sits in the Yangming channel and does not disperse, forming membranous distension.

Pressing on it: the chest and diaphragm have soft, vacuous, or substantial membrane distension from heat. When the membrane is dry and the heat does not subside, the fullness reduces internally. Those whose pain worsens upon pressure are of the excess-heat type; those whose pain is relieved by warmth are of the cold-deficiency type. When the abdomen is hard and the fullness does not reduce upon pressure, this too is cold-deficiency — warmth is appropriate. Water distension in the membrane: the membrane cavity and the four limbs swell below with severe edema. This is located in the Taiyin and Yangming channels; abdominal qi congests and rises.

Dongui Bogam, Volume One (continued)

脈法

腹脹帶不減絕不足者脈洪數。脈盛而緊為脹。日浮為虛。

其脈滿大而緊則內脹。弦而緊則可治。滿而緊大而緊則虛。脹小則難保。虛則脹緊流諸者閉。上脈或弦虛。

氣兩進大腹浮淳。或中運實而淳則可察者小也。虛則細諸緊流者閉。上脈或弦虛。

脹病有七

面水黑脹是氣鼓脹皮膚者皆在虛脹府之外。拌寒脹而郭胃脹脅脹。

血鼓脹黑脹是氣鼓血膿脹滿亦有血。其身上有膿惡經臟腑脹是痛其膿。

成是鹹疝散為去清水作。是水鼓腹膨脹問小。腎腹膨脹是食鼓脹有。堵惡如寒鼓手者足。

寒脹

利者腹脹冷滿時減。宜溫之補土。

熟脹

熟者脈必浮數。浮則陽為虛數。則陽盛。虛則陰虛數。則陽盛生外熟。陰虛不能宣導內。
translation:
Pulse Method

When abdominal distension accompanies a pulse that does not diminish or cease and is insufficient, the pulse will be surging and rapid. When the pulse is full and wiry, it indicates distension. A floating pulse indicates vacuity.

When the pulse is full, large, and tight, there is internal distension. When it is wiry and tight, the condition is treatable. When full, tight, large, and tight together, there is vacuity. When distension is slight, the prognosis is difficult to maintain. When vacuous, distension is accompanied by tight flow; those that are blocked have an upper pulse that is either wiry or vacuous.

When qi advances and the abdomen is large and floating with stagnation — or when there is internal movement and solidity with stagnation — those that can be examined are small. When vacuous, the fine pulse flows tightly; those blocked have an upper pulse that is wiry or vacuous.

Seven Types of Abdominal Distension

Facial water-black distension (water drum distension) — qi drum distension in which the skin and all areas are in the external region of the vacuous distension bowels and viscera. Differentiated are cold distension, stomach distension, and rib distension.

Blood drum distension — black distension is qi drum with blood and pus distension; full with blood as well. The body above has pus; the visceral distension is painful with pus.

Formed from salty hernia dispersal — after removing clear water it forms. This is water drum distension with a small abdomen. Kidney abdominal distension is food drum distension. [There are also blocked and malignant types like cold drum with extremity involvement.]

Cold Distension

In cold distension, the abdominal distension is cold and full but reduces from time to time. It is appropriate to warm and supplement the earth (spleen).

Heat Distension

In heat distension, the pulse must be floating and rapid. Floating indicates yang vacuity with rapidity. Rapid indicates exuberant yang. Vacuity indicates yin vacuity with rapidity. Exuberant yang generates external heat. Yin vacuity fails to disseminate and conduct internally.

translation:
Grain Distension (Grain Bloating):
When food and drink are consumed as usual but the abdomen becomes distended, appetite is lost, food cravings arise, and then yin grows while yang diminishes. In the morning it is difficult to digest; therefore yang cannot restrain the qi, which easily becomes stored up.

Water Distension:
Fluids collect in the body as dampness invades; there is a sound of water, and the water remains stagnant. The skin frequently suffers from this condition, and relief cannot be obtained.

Qi Distension:
Seven out of ten cases present with restlessness of the body, softness of the limbs, water swelling, and hardening. The four pathways of great qi are blocked; breathing is difficult; qi cannot descend; the abdomen distends below; the bowels are stupefied and cannot move.

Blood Distension:
There is great vexation; the stools are black; water retreats and the person is averse to eating; there is frequent fright and mania, painful blockage, and vomiting of blood; urination is difficult.

Treatment of Distension and Fullness:
One must treat the heat of distension carefully. If there is internal cold, the medicines must be thick and warm; the abdomen requires supplementing. When fullness is great, one must already act to dispel dampness. In cases of cold distension with fullness and much heat, one treats accordingly.

If transformation fails and the physician does not investigate the source of the disease, seeking quick results, the patient suffers distension that suddenly seems to improve — this is a dangerous sign.

One must regulate and promote the wood phase, seek proper technique, and use methods to dredge and regulate the kidney, supplement water, preserve the lung qi, and obtain the metal phase through calming.

One must use Ginseng (參) and White Atractylodes (白朮), assisted by Tangerine Peel (陳皮) to move qi rapidly.

translation:
Drum Distension (Gu Zhang)
Shixie Powder (Feces and Vinegar Powder)

[Formula for treating] various types of drum distension: this formula treats cold-heat type gu distension. The powder addresses heat in the blood. Commonly it is said that one should individually assess patients — those who are full after eating, use White Atractylodes (Baizhu); those with mature distension, use Baizhu; those with damp overflow, use Cangzhu (Gray Atractylodes) and Magnolia Bark (Houpu).

Using medicines for quick profit seeking a momentary relief — one does not realize that this provides no lasting benefit even for half a day. Those who recover from drum distension are those who do not seek a quick cure but rather understand that the root is deep, the true qi has been impaired, and one must seek treatment from afar.

It is appropriate to use qi-regulating formulas; use large doses of water-draining agents; use Zhishi, Houpu (Magnolia Bark), and cut Wangdao.

The dampness draining approach promotes water flow. The nine orifices and eyes show signs; seeking quick results requires self-administration. The skin and membranes, together — one should...

Against this: correspondence with Bencao answers — pale in color, like stone stream; compared to white it is slightly lighter in qi. The qi distension — commonly said to be abdominal fullness; individually assess: those who are full, use Renshen (Ginseng) and Baizhu; for ripe/mature distension use Baizhu; for damp overflow use Cangzhu and Houpu.

Also there is a formula that cuts off cold, reduces water, disperses heat qi, and treats gu distension.

[Composition]: Various ingredients including willow bark, yellow fine powder, two qian, taken with ginger decoction three times, adjusted with Shengma (Cimicifuga) juice; each time take one fang of chicken droppings on an empty stomach, drink; one large dose of ginger and peach kernel (Taoren), each one sheng, divided; the right side [treats] purulent water distension; mix and stir-fry with aromatics.

Turbid Qi Rising Causes Abdominal Distension

When turbid qi rises upward, it produces membrane distension (bloating). Cold fullness accumulates in the upper region. When the first burner is affected, the refined essence of food and drink cannot be transformed and distributed; instead it congeals and becomes coarse. This turbid qi is a form of cold-turbid qi. It moves along the yang pathways upward and gives rise to conditions. Afterward, the patient suffers from abdominal distension, and at night the qi cannot flow freely, which ultimately harms the patient's vitality. The key point is that this turbid qi is the root cause of the condition, and it ascends. Wood (liver) first regulates qi in the abdomen, as reflected in the bowstring and tight pulse. The decoction treats sinking and stagnation, using aromatics and Jiao Tai formula with pills.

Moxiang Shunqi Tang (Aucklandia Qi-Regulating Decoction)

Bupleurum (Chaihu) 5 fen, Licorice (Gancao) each portion, Alpinia oxyphylla (Yizhi) each portion, Evodia (Wuzhuyu) each 3 fen, Aucklandia root (Muxiang), Dried ginger (Ganjiang) each 1 qian, Fresh ginger 3 slices, decoct and take; Angelica root (Danggui) 8 fen, Codonopsis and Atractylodes each portion.

Each Shaoyang and Yangming, second pathway, dispersing and clearing qi — with acrid moving, ascending yang, used as chief with bitter, sweet, acrid, greatly warm herbs to disperse and smooth middle burner stagnant cold qi.

Danggui, Renshen (Ginseng), Muxiang (Aucklandia), Cangzhu (Atractylodes), Qingpi (Green tangerine peel), Fuling (Poria), Gancao (Licorice), Zexie (Alisma), Bohe (Mint) — guards and nourishes qi, guides and leads turbid qi, regulates qi, manages the broad qi dynamic; for those with thin yang in the middle, Chenpi (Tangerine peel) and Fuling, Gancao, Zexie, Bohe protect the qi.

The yin qi descends from heaven downward, and therefore it is considered turbid qi; since it does not descend, bitter [herbs] are used to drain it.

The qi of Evodia (Wu Zhuyu) rises from below upward, and therefore it is used as an assistant [herb]; it causes the turbid qi to combine flavors and disperse.

Wu Zhuyu Decoction (Evodia Decoction): Treats dampness in the chest and diaphragm. [Ingredients:] Magnolia bark, fresh ginger, cinnamon. When true yin is exuberant and cold, with abdominal fullness and distension.

[It] secures each [element] in its proper position, allowing the clear and turbid to be [regulated] accordingly.

[Each ingredient addresses] fullness, distension, and qi in the membranes; when food and drink are impaired and yin is exuberant with cold causing true abdominal fullness.

[Preparation:] One cover, combined with water, decocted. Take [dose of] white [herb] or aged tangerine peel powder, Sichuan pepper, stir-fried, five fen each, right side [dose], take Wu Zhuyu Decoction, serving as pills, dried.

Sinking Fragrance Blending Elixir (Chen Xiang Jiao Tai Wan)

[Ingredients:] Aquilaria (Chen Xiang), [other ingredients] formed into pills with steamed cake binder. For cold damage, details found in the formulary. Pills the size of a parasol tree seed, taken warm with water, sending down: aquilaria, green [herb], aquilaria, evodia, white [herb], aged tangerine peel, rhubarb — grind all into powder.

Abdominal fullness and distension in cold damage and febrile disease is a true visceral disorder.

Abdominal fullness and distension being a true visceral disorder arises from gastric duct fatigue and fullness; this too is natural, as the viscera store the true [qi]. When the viscera are diseased, it is as if one's illness is reversed.

True wood stores itself; when not diseased, the five phases mutually restrain — water restrains, appropriately balancing. Even without taking medicine [it may resolve].

When both wood [elements] heal themselves, if disease rises, metal restrains metal; water and fire generate earth, generating earth, thus the palace controls. Though there are also antagonistic and contraindicated medicines, life may still continue — this is what is meant by the saying, for it is understood that [the system regulates itself].

Simple Remedies

Magnolia Bark (Houpo): For treating abdominal fullness and distension. Use slices of magnolia bark, decocted together. Take only the liquid. For cases where there is knotting and accumulation, decoct and make a powder. Take five to six doses. Use five qian (a unit of weight) in a decoction. This will bring about recovery. Euphorbia (Daji): Used alongside sliced pieces to treat abdominal fullness. Take one dou (unit of measure) of the decoction with a large date. The flavor is acrid. One piece inside, five doses, taken so as to disperse accumulations and bring about recovery.

Eagle/Vulture Droppings: For treating post-partum [conditions]. Thoroughly effective. According to Gong [a physician], the body turns yellow inside with abdominal distension. Grind into powder, stir-fry until white, take with warm wine, seven doses. Eagle and vulture [droppings] — warm water, mix and take. This is from the Han [tradition].

Toad: Yellow broth, with membranes and various dried membranes. Extract the juice. Dry the fungus into powder, stir-fry, take with wine, seven pieces. Eagle and vulture — warm. This is it.

Chicken Droppings: Yellow, broth, with membranes and various dried membranes. Extract the juice. Grind into powder, stir-fry. Take with wine, seven pieces.

[General discussion:] Clearing. Three major [conditions] of the abdomen — counterflow, blood. The pulse is large; the abdomen is large. At four times, one is cut off from clear [qi]. The four counterflows — these are the forms.

If one can benefit the diaphragm and treat [the condition], if the heart and abdomen are not [settled], there is agitation. This is a case of chronic illness with emaciation, sudden diarrhea and convulsions. Membranes are visible, fullness is extreme; recovery depends on breathing and [whether the patient can] bear it. With expansion [of the condition], treatment is possible.

Treating abdominal fullness: if there is no resolution, or if urination is not possible, or if there is no warmth, and the abdomen is greatly distended — this cannot be treated.
