translation:
消渴 (Wasting-Thirst / Diabetes)

The Origins of Wasting-Thirst

The Inner Canon (Neijing) states: "When the two yang become bound, this is called wasting-thirst (xiao)." The two yang refers to Yangming. Yangming binding means heat stored in the stomach and intestines. The commentary says: "One yang binding means both the stomach and large intestine are bound by heat together." Yangming governs the stomach; the diseases generated by the stomach — when there is heat there is yellowing, dry mouth, tendency to consume large amounts of water, and insufficiency of fluids, causing thirst.

When the hand Yangming and foot Yangming are deficient in fire, the large intestine tends toward binding of blood; fluids and humors are insufficient, causing scorching thirst, as if burned by fire; the foot [meridian] binds and does not moisten, hence the tendency toward wasting.

All of this is dryness of blood and internal heat with lurking fire. When blood cannot circulate in its domain, the fluids become like fire, not moistening, and one who drinks once and dies is the wasting-thirst pattern.

The treatment involves needling and moxibustion: needling or moxibustion at Sanli (ST-36) — this is the key point of the pulse. Also take Sanli and Wangu points.

At 8–2 cun and a half, or moxa with fifty cones — this is the essential point of the vessels. Also take Sanlii and Wangu.

[The text discusses that wasting-thirst arises from the lung, stomach, and kidney; that those who overindulge in rich, sweet foods and fatty meats tend to develop this disease; and that the wealthy and noble are especially prone to it.]

translation:
Manifestations and Symptoms of Wasting-Thirst (Xiaoke/消渴)

The transformation into wasting-thirst disorder: The commentary states that those who eat fatty foods have dense skin and interstices, so yang qi cannot disperse outward; those who drink sweet things cause the spleen's qi to overflow upward, transforming into wasting-thirst. Hence the craving for sweet things externally.

Because fatty and sweet foods by nature flare upward, the spleen's upper qi overflows, and so drinking transforms into wasting-thirst, causing frequent urination; when urination is reduced, it becomes scanty.

When there is dryness and fullness in the middle, yang qi produces internal heat; excess drinking leads to overflow of spleen qi upward, thus transforming into wasting-thirst.

There are three forms of wasting disorder: wasting-thirst (消渴), wasting of the middle (消中), and wasting of the kidney (消腎). Internal heat in the kidney steams upward into the stomach and upper burner, causing vexation and dryness.

When heart fire is excessive, one drinks frequently but cannot rapidly digest fluids — this is wasting of the middle (消中). When the stomach is vacuous and hot, heat fumes upward causing frequent urination.

This heat dissolves the flesh; vacuity-heat fumigates and steams, blocking the free flow of fluids.

Wasting of the kidney involves vacuity below, with fluids descending to nourish themselves; the kidney becomes vacuous and urination becomes frequent and uncontrolled.

The legs become withered, the bones and joints ache and waste, and the condition worsens. This belongs to the category of vacuity with downward-drawing of fluids.

Those who originally retained kidney function but then cut off yang pathways — strong yang with no outlet — along with those who consume the five minerals: in such persons, true qi is consumed and wasting-thirst is exhausted to the point of forming stones.

In wasting of the middle, one may temporarily manage with frequent water intake, but recovery is slow and the condition should not be taken lightly.

Wasting of the upper burner involves the lungs; it is also called strong wasting of the middle, with great thirst and frequent drinking, with little urination — do not treat this lightly.

translation:
Page 85 — On Wasting-Thirst (消渴, Xiao Ke / Diabetes-like conditions)

TYPES OF DISCHARGE / URINE:
Normal urine that is clear, the ears turn black, the body becomes thin, and there is greenish oil in the urine — this is Lower Wasting (下消). Upper Wasting (上消) involves drinking much water. Middle Wasting (中消) involves the stomach; one eats much but the face becomes small/thin.

PULSE METHOD (脈法):
In wasting-thirst, the pulse should be large — if the patient is at ease, it is treatable. If the pulse is large and rapid, tight and full, it can be treated. If the pulse is sunken, fine, and short, the prognosis is death over time. If it is faint and small, death follows gradually. If there are masses (癥), it cannot be cured.

ON THE CONDITION:
When one drinks much water but urinates little, and the qi is in the eyes — then the back becomes cold, fluids are consumed, saliva is chewed dry, and one drinks little: this is because of deficiency-thirst. Therefore wasting occurs. The five viscera are all involved in wasting because of thirst-deficiency. In wasting-thirst, the pulse is large and rapid; the Large Yang (太陽) pulse, if vigorous and small, means the stomach heat is consuming. The heart pulse being slippery and large means the stool will be hard and the urine will be abnormal (跌) — this is wasting-thirst. If the heart pulse is faint and small, it is clear masses (清癥).

THREE TYPES OF WASTING-THIRST (消渴有三):
[Treatments listed:]
- Jiangzi Decoction (降子湯) — for those unable to descend
- Renshen Shigao (人參石膏) — clear-heart lotus seed drink (清心蓮子飲)
- Harmonize blood and benefit qi decoction (和血益氣湯)

Additional formulas: Shenling Baizhu San (參苓白朮散) — also treats thirst with white [discharge]. Flavored Red Poria Decoction (加味赤茯苓湯) — for great thirst with excessive drinking, emaciation, cracked lips. Upper [wasting] with great thirst, one should use small amounts; if the pulse is fine and rapid with great thirst, the stool will be hard and the urine abnormal.

七末十欲下五
內胃經核熟大腸粺熟日及胃㑊註日㑊易也飲食㑊

易而過不生肌膚也消中亦熟日食㑊善食而瘦易又謂之食㑊

治法與消渴同須以明物

下甜入骨髓在膀胱若若腸色黃血之餘又不能五吹上不能

藏為化氣肉鹹其畫調肺老為五厚桔故盡蓋也味若甘甜不

蒸為化色氣清肺其畫調肺老為五厚桔故盡蓋也味若甘甜不下有暖

煦氣蒸則肺而

消渴小便甜

消渴由坎火衰少

愛蒸化色氣清肺調下老為五公桔故盡蓋也若甘甜不下有暖不能升氣蒸乾而肺

升則此板終不得滋火力者腰腎强感常須煎慶補腎

升故成乾白百坤故其下如能封中為有否陽無火水之陰降故以板陽覆不

translation:
Signs of Food Dissipation (食㑊)

Food dissipation refers to a condition where one eats well but grows thin. It is also called dietary dissipation (食㑊). The treatment method is the same as for consumptive thirst (消渴), and one must use appropriate substances.

Although one eats, the food does not build muscle and flesh. The condition involves urinary difficulty and exhaustion, so that the urine becomes sweet. From this we understand: when the kidney is deficient, the urine becomes sweet; when it is excessive, it becomes like a clear stream.

Sweetness penetrates into the bone marrow and into the bladder. If the small intestine's color is yellow — being the residue of blood — it cannot transform to saltiness, so the urine becomes yellow. When the small intestine's color is yellow and blood's residue cannot transform, the urine becomes sweet.

After eating, if the qi of food cannot be transformed into salty flavor, it instead becomes sweet urine. The kidney qi, when excessive, produces this condition.

The qi of steaming and transformation: the lungs govern the regulation of qi; if the lungs are weakened and cannot descend, the warming qi cannot rise, the steaming dries out, and the lungs suffer.

Consumptive Thirst with Sweet Urine (消渴小便甜)

Consumptive Thirst Arising from Deficiency of Kidney Fire (消渴由坎火衰少)

When the transformative steaming of the body's qi cannot properly regulate the lungs, and the descending function fails, there is insufficient warmth and the rising qi cannot steam properly, leading to dryness in the lungs.

If this rising function fails, fluids cannot be produced; fire energy wanes; the lumbar region and kidneys weaken; one must then tonify and supplement the kidneys.

When dryness prevails and the earth element (坤) cannot seal and contain properly, the yang qi fails to descend; fire and water become imbalanced; yin cannot descend and yang cannot rise, resulting in thirst.

Five-Bean Decoction (五豆湯)
Ingredients: Black soybeans, ginger, licorice root (each cut), green beans, red beans, small beans — each one jin (斤). Take the right amount. Use five mal (斗) of water, seal in a ceramic vessel. Bitterwood Decoction (苦練湯)
Take three portions of the parasitic worm [medicine], boil as a decoction. Treat the condition, benefiting [the patient]. Boil down to one cup, empty the heart [stomach]. The liquid from the bitterwood (苦練) root end — its bitter juice: although the meat, when charred and combined with a little perilla-fragrance herb, does not cause harm — add a small amount of water afterward.

Worm-Thirst (蟲渴)
[A condition caused by worms producing thirst.]

Strong-Center Syndrome (強中證)
Drinking and eating excessively — because of [this], having four or five [symptoms], [the condition] is rooted [in the body]. The complexion becomes overall flushed, moisture and fluids [are depleted], skin [suffers], and though one drinks frequently, one knows [the thirst is not quenched]. Though [yang] qi is vigorous on the surface, the true qi has already collapsed; pathogenic yang is dominant and aroused [uncontrollably].

Transformed Complications of Wasting-Thirst (Xiaoke)

[Discusses how the condition changes and transforms:] If lower wasting develops, adding scallion root and white [atractylodes], or if the disease has not yet progressed to itching sores, this is the reason. Using the powder formula, adding or reducing [herbs] to treat it, using the white atractylodes powder in the upper and middle [burners].

For elderly people who must eat, if the disease spreads to the middle [stage] where the patient can eat excessively, swelling and complications will develop. For those who are in the complicated and closed stage, reducing treatment is possible; if the patient is able to take doses, all of these are untreatable conditions with a rigid spine.

translation:
Prohibitions and Contraindications

The Inner Classic states: In heat-wasting disorder (cooked-center type), one must not take millet, fragrant herbs, or mineral drugs. In the middle-wasting disorder, one must not drink alcohol. For those engaged in sexual activity, though they eat, they will not feel full. Things stored within the body — sour and salty foods — may also aggravate the wasting condition. In the ninth stage of wasting, great thirst increases day by day.

Contraindications: One must not drink alcohol. The illness requires caution; there are three types of drugs: first, those that cannot be taken; second, acupuncture and moxibustion must be applied with care; third, salty foods should be avoided. This aggravates wasting.

Upper [type of wasting]: If one is not yet dying, iron-based moxibustion will cause sores to suppurate and the pus-water will not stop. Strongly contraindicated are Pinellia (半夏), Arisaema (南星), and drying agents.

Four types. For nineteen conditions combined: use glutinous rice, cook and take the decoction of Dendrobium (玉斛), drink accordingly.

Single Remedies

Gypsum (石膏): Mainly treats wasting-thirst. Grind to powder, measure out and drink a measure of Dendrobium decoction.

Bamboo Leaves (竹葉): Stop vexation and clear heat. Measure the decoction and drink.

Talcum (滑石): Regulates and treats downward wasting-thirst. Use immediately — combine with the above powder, mix as Yuanmo Han Qing San. Three names: take with plain water or honey water.

Earth Slurry (地漿): Treats heat in the stomach, heart vexation, and trembling. Take the marvelous preparation.

Bamboo Sap (竹瀝): Publicly treats thirst; also treats heart vexation and agitation. It is suitable to take and drink. Dry Bamboo Sap is the marvelous preparation.

Ophiopogon Root (麥門冬): Remove the center, boil into a decoction, and drink it.

Coptis (Huang Lian): Treats wasting-thirst (diabetes-like condition); it is the essential medicine. Take seventy pills of Jade Hairpin Flower, dried and chewed, for a wonderful effect.

Mulberry Twig Tea (Sang Zhi Cha): Take regularly for best results; take Korean dried tea and chew.

translation:
Mulberry Root Bark (Sang Geun Baek Pi)
Mulberry root bark primarily treats heat and thirst, and replenishes vital essence. Place it in honey, boil and drink. Also, pound black mulberries, filter out the sediment, place in a stone pot and cook down to a paste; take 2–3 spoonfuls dissolved in boiling water each time. Stops thirst.

Oyster Meat (Moran)
Oyster meat, eaten raw, treats thirst. Commonly known as "stone flower." It is best boiled and eaten, or eaten raw mixed with ginger and vinegar.

Freshwater Clams (Banghap)
Freshwater clams primarily treat wasting-thirst (消渴). For the three types of wasting-thirst, use as a dietary remedy: take the extract, combine with powdered coptis (yellow-connect) and form into pills. Also, boil river snails and drink the broth for good results.

Catfish (Jeom Eo)
Catfish primarily treats wasting-thirst. Decoct and take the liquid; combine with powdered coptis and form into pills.

River Snail (Jeon Ra)
River snail: drink the juice to treat thirst. Each day it facilitates urination. Combine with honey water; soak snails in one dou of water overnight, take the liquid and drink. Good results.

Raw Lotus Root (Saeng U)
Raw lotus root juice treats thirst. Take a portion; it facilitates frequent urination. Combined with honey water, also boil river snails and drink the broth for good results.

Red Persimmon (Hong Si)
Red persimmon treats thirst. Facilitates urination. Combined with honey water; soak in one dou of water overnight, take the liquid and drink. Good results.

Black Plum (O Mae)
Black plum: decoct with a small amount of dried honey; regularly resolves wasting-thirst.

Pear (I)
Pear: eating it stops wasting-thirst. Take and treat the center; reduces thirst consistently.

translation:
Kiwi fruit (Mihutao): Relieves thirst. For thirst, take fruit that has ripened after frost, mix with small amount of white [ingredient], decoct and take the juice as a drink.

Schisandra berry (Five-flavor fruit): Relieves thirst. For thirst, steam and sun-dry nine times, eat as food, make into pills and take regularly. Also, boil the seeds, pound them finely, take one sheng of the kernels, pound until soft, take the juice as a drink; or dry in vinegar and drink regularly.

Hemp seed: For treating thirst from drinking alcohol — boil and clarify, take one sheng of kernels, pound until soft and good, take the juice as a drink; or dry with vinegar and drink regularly.

Millet water (grain-washing water): Treat wasting-thirst disorder — take the liquid from rinsing millet, or clarified liquid is best; drink the juice. If left too long it turns sour; drink regularly.

Sorghum (Gaoliang) rice: Grind and extract juice to treat wasting-thirst; boil in water or cook as rice and take the cooking liquid as a regular food drink.

Green sorghum rice: Good for relieving heat and wasting-thirst; cook as rice, take the cooking liquid as a drink.

Glutinous rice: Good for relieving wasting and thirst — wash the rice, take the ash from rice straw, steep in hot water, remove the lye, take the inner portion, [process] to make a white liquid; this treats wasting-thirst.

Winter melon: Take [the melon], burn or cook it in various ways, take regularly as food and drink.
Also: make into a vine-preparation, take as a powder with food and drink.
Also: excellent for clearing heat and relieving thirst — if taken with glutinous rice liquid, steep in hot water, clarify and remove sediment.

translation:
Waterweed (Brasenia schreberi): It is mainly used to treat wasting-thirst (消渴, diabetes-like condition). It can be made into soup or pickles, and eaten regularly. It is also suitable eaten as is.

Rooster Broth: It is mainly used for treatment. Take the broth and drink it regularly. It may also be eaten as food. The illness will recede. One cup of clear rooster broth drunk as a beverage.

White Goose Juice: Drink the juice, use it as a clear liquid; boil until cooked and take the broth. Boiling it thoroughly is also suitable for drinking.

Yellow Hen: It is mainly used to clear [heat]. Drink the liquid; use it as a clear liquid. Boil until cooked and take the broth. The meat may also be eaten hot, and the broth drunk.

Cow's Milk: It is mainly used to treat wasting-thirst. Take the curds or fresh milk; it is also suitable as a drink.

Pig's Stomach: Stop [wasting-thirst]. Mainly used to relieve thirst. Take and steam it, combine with fresh milk; it is also a suitable drink.

Jaundice

The Causes of Jaundice: The classics say: When damp-heat and other factors interact, the disease, though purely a yang type with no yin [factor], manifests as yellow [coloration]. When urination is difficult, blood stagnates and yellowing develops with inhibited urination.

If it settles in the lower burner, heat merely consumes the blood without consuming the body fluids, so urination remains uninhibited.

When [damp-heat] settles in the lower burner, heat consumes the body fluids, causing inhibited urination.

translation:
There are Five Types of Jaundice (Huang Dan)

When excessive earth-qi accumulates and stagnates without resolution, it transforms into cold-water retention, causing the most critical situation where the person cannot eat or drink; the yin aspect collapses entirely. Cold disease develops around the ninth day during seasonal epidemics and febrile illnesses, and if purged downward, yellow [jaundice] develops.

Yellow [jaundice with] thirst and desire to drink: the patient cannot obtain water; the urine is yellow and scanty. This will inevitably end with cold and heat in the four limbs, dampness and heat accumulating, the abdomen distended, the facial pulse sunken and indistinct.

This is related to disinhibiting urination. Red jaundice arises from jade (dietary) causes; the condition is the same as muscle and flesh cold-damp heat combining, hence [jaundice occurs].

According to classic texts: at the eighth to tenth day of illness, when sweating should occur during the expected period, if the patient labors and eats instead, no sweat is produced, causing the name "Yellow" disease. The liver and gallbladder are responsible; it is called jaundice disease — this refers to the condition where one should disinhibit urination; if prolonged and uncured [it worsens].

When heat develops, yellowing of the body occurs. Running through five pathways equally, the body develops this condition from accumulation of dampness-heat steaming together, affecting the blood.

The five types of jaundice disease are: first, Yellow Jaundice (huang dan); second, Alcohol Jaundice (jiu dan); third, Hunger Jaundice (ji dan) involving the stomach; fourth, Red Jaundice (chi dan), with redness and yellowing of the eyes, slight yellowing — this is called Yellow Jaundice with a melon-seed (jaundiced) yellow complexion; fifth, Female Labor disease (nü lao bing), with yellow eyes, yellowish complexion, multiple yellowing from cold disease, with excessive water retention.

translation:
Yellow Jaundice (Huangdan):
This condition involves heat retained internally, causing the urine, face, eyes, teeth, and limbs to turn yellow like gold. It arises from sudden exposure to heat followed by bathing in cold water while hungry.

Alcohol Jaundice (Jiudan):
This disease is caused by alcohol triggering jaundice. The patient feels uneasy at heart, with a constant urge to urinate, a sensation of distress and heat, inability to eat, heat in the chest, and heat in the soles of the feet. This is called alcohol jaundice. The patient desires to vomit, experiences heat below, and craves drink. Alcohol jaundice resembles malaria in its recurring nature.

Grain Jaundice (Gudan):
The patient frequently wants to eat and drink, but has difficulty with urination, and the spleen and stomach feel full. The nature of jaundice as a disease involves alternating chills and fever, loss of appetite, and after eating, dizziness and discomfort in the chest. If the condition persists too long with great hunger, it worsens.

Female Taxation Jaundice (Nülaodan):
This arises from overexertion, leading to jaundice with discoloration. It is called female taxation jaundice. Symptoms include fullness, distress in the heart, cold feet, emaciation and thinness, with outbreaks of abdominal distension and acute swelling.

Yellow Sweat (Huanghan):
The sweat turns yellow; upon bathing in water the condition is acquired. Gradually the sweat stains clothing a true yellow color. The patient is not thirsty.

Yellow Sweat (further description):
In this form of yellow sweat disease, the body swells, fever develops, sweating occurs with thirst, and the sweat stains the clothing.

translation:
Pulse Method
Section 5: In jaundice with a excess pulse — a tight, surging pulse is normal; a wiry pulse may also occur; a faint, floating pulse indicates various conditions that should be treated carefully, as this relates to spiritual debility.

Methods for Treating Yellow Jaundice (Huangdan)
Jaundice with excess: use cold [natured medicines]. Various jaundice conditions should be treated according to whether urination is free or difficult; when urination is free, prolonged taxation leads to a condition where urine becomes white or colorless — this is not the type that can be purged with heat-clearing methods; rather, one should use heat and dampness [clearing methods]. For various jaundice conditions that do not disperse with surface-releasing methods, the interior must be treated, for there is no other approach.

Promote urination. If vomiting or sweating occurs, use diaphoresis or emesis as appropriate. When the skin turns yellow like smoke-color, or yellow-orange like a ripe tangerine — when the whole body is entirely yellow and orange-colored — and the patient is jaundiced due to food [accumulation].

For damp-type disease: when the whole body is yellow like smoke, or bright yellow like a ripe tangerine, use rhubarb (Dahuang) to purge. When the yellow naturally recedes, the treatment of jaundice is complete. Jaundice arising from food [accumulation].

For accumulation-type: first treat the root condition; the remaining [formula]: take the ingredients, grind to fine powder; Rhubarb (Dahuang) dry-fried warm, 1 liang; Yellow tea, 2 qian.

Huanglian San (Coptis Powder)
Take three times daily. First use Licorice (Gancao), [various ingredients] each one [liang]; grind to fine powder; Rhubarb (Dahuang) stir-fried warm, mix with water and take, divided into two doses.

This medicine is used externally: take fresh ginger and melon-pedicle (Digua), pound and squeeze out the juice, rub onto the skin; take half a dou, decoct with good wine half a sheng, divided doses; in winter use wine, in spring and summer use water, measured to the appropriate amount.

Mahuang Chunjiu Tang (Ephedra and Pure Wine Decoction)
Remove [unwanted parts], decoct Ephedra (Mahuang) together, pound until soft and extract the juice; in winter use good wine half a sheng; in spring and summer use water, measured to the appropriate amount.

translation:
Alcohol Jaundice is the Most Serious

Among the five types of jaundice, alcohol jaundice produces the most varied and dangerous complications. Alcohol, being a substance that generates heat and toxic accumulation, seeps into the hundred vessels throughout the body. It does not merely cause yellowing of the skin; the yellow coloration spreads and intensifies. In those who appear to recover, the toxin penetrates the skin and turns it black, or causes great swelling; the pathogen enters the channels, and if not stopped, the eyes turn yellow and the yellowing persists.

The condition differs in presentation from other types. It is of the same category as kidney-related disorders. There is a form called "Black Jaundice," also known as "Taxing Exhaustion" (Wenláo), in which the body is cold and the skin turns yellow.

Black Jaundice is Difficult to Treat

This condition commonly affects women who have contracted it through association with kidney disease. The pattern of Black Jaundice presents with fever in the late afternoon (around 3–5 pm), lower abdominal fullness, and the entire body turning yellow or black. The forehead and head turn black like water stains. Treatment uses fumigation with garlic; prolonged cases may be due to irregular bowel movements.

In some cases urination is difficult; in others the pulse is tight and thin, hollow and vacuous — this indicates cold accumulation throughout the body, causing hardness and fullness below the heart, which can transform into Yin Jaundice.

Yin Jaundice

Suitable formulas include Artemisia (Yinchen) decoctions. When Yang excess occurs in conjunction with Taiyin channel tightness and vacuity, cold pervades the body, causing epigastric hardness and transforming into Yin Jaundice. Treatment should include Yinchen, Fuzi (aconite), and Ganjiang (dried ginger) decoction, along with formulas to address the accompanying symptoms.

Formula One:
Treats jaundice.
Ingredients: Peony root (1 qian), Aged tangerine peel, Turmeric, Agarwood, Sugar (5 fen), White Atractylodes.
Preparation: Slice the ingredients, decoct in water until thoroughly cooked, divide into portions and take orally.

[Measurements: 9, 5, 1 cun/slices — stir-fry one slice, stir-fry over raw powder, use taro root powder with honey, roast until done, take on an empty stomach.]

Treatable and Untreatable Conditions:

In treating jaundice, ten to eighteen days is the critical period; cases difficult to treat need not be abandoned — those who show signs of improvement within this period may still be treated.

When treatment is regulated and the condition involves fever with swelling, and the yellowing is found in the lower abdominal region, if the patient's pulse is near the yin region, the case may be treatable.

When the patient shows no visual response, the tongue is stiff, the nostrils and heart region turn completely black, and the facial color turns dark like a lotus flower blackened — such cases may still attempt treatment but prognosis is poor.

When there is fever and swelling, and the yellowing is in the stomach region, if the pulse is near the yang region within eighteen days, the case may be treatable.

When there is irritability, thirst, and a black facial complexion with sores, and after eighteen days the stomach and spleen show signs of exhaustion — if there is slight improvement, treatment may be attempted.

In cases of alcohol-induced jaundice where the face is black, the skin yellow with eruptions, and the abdomen is hard and distended — such cases are difficult to treat.

translation:
Simple Remedies

Wine: boil nine kinds of three decoctions. There are varieties with mild [effects].

Bile and Snow Water: warm, treats jaundice; desired effect of yellowing the skin, pound [the ingredient].

Plantain (Che Qian Cao): Take the most [effective part] to treat jaundice. Boil with concentrated water, drink. This is called "wine-boiled." For redness in the urine with yellowing of the skin and face, boil with concentrated water and consume, either as a decoction or eaten raw.

Artemisia (Yin Chen Hao): Also primarily treats [jaundice]. Good for treating it. Clears and treats yellowing symptoms. Take one liang, decoct with clear water, and drink.

Kudzu Root (Ge Gen): Take one portion to resolve alcohol [toxicity] and jaundice. Boil in water; for redness in urine and yellowing of the face and body, soak [in water].

Snake Gourd Herb (Gua Lou Cao): Primarily [used with] water, decoct eight [portions], take regularly. The root is very bitter; pound [it].

Physalis Root (Suan Jiang Gen): Primarily collects [and treats] jaundice. Pound [the root], take the juice frequently, and drink.

Dandelion Root (Dang Cao Gen): Also primarily [treats] heartburn and jaundice. For those who have it, pound and extract the juice. Take one sheng [unit of measure]. If there is yellow water in the abdomen, take the root, pound it, extract the juice; if it does not subside, [repeat] again on an empty stomach.

Taking Medicines

Artemisia (青蒿): Treats heat jaundice. Extract the juice and drink it. For heart pain, pound it.

Knotweed (篇蓄): Treats jaundice when taken as a drink. Pound a small amount and extract the juice, take one升 (unit of measure).

Young barley shoots (大麥苗): Extract the juice and take it as the primary treatment for jaundice. Can also be prepared as a gruel mixed with other things. Take daily. Easy to obtain living specimens. Saves many people.

Carp (鯉魚): For treating jaundice, prepare using the usual method.

Egret (鷺): For treating egret jaundice, make into wine and consume. Take multiple doses as usual.

translation:
Peach Root
Treats jaundice with yellowing of the body and face as if golden in color. Take a handful of peach roots growing toward the east, cut them finely like water reeds, decoct in clear rice wine until concentrated. Strain and take the wine on a half-empty stomach. After one day, the jaundice will gradually disperse.

Turnip Seeds (Mastic Greens Seeds)
Category: Outgoing/Differential
Mainly treats acute jaundice. Take two or three qian dissolved in warm water and administer. Insert the powder into both nostrils. Also, this draws out and resolves stagnation in the abdomen and obstructed bowels. Take the seeds, grind finely, mix with chive and calcined arsenolite herb, burn finely.

Sweet Melon Pedicel (Melon Stem)
Category: Outgoing/Differential
Treats jaundice at initial onset and seasonal acute jaundice. Use melon pedicel as powder, insert into both nostrils to draw out yellow fluid. Also take one qian dissolved in warm water to induce vomiting of yellow fluid, which brings relief.

Luffa (Silk Gourd)
Category: Korean Differential
Treats jaundice from alcohol and wheat/flour excess. Burn the luffa vine and skin and seeds to ash, make into powder. Take several doses dissolved in wine; the illness resolves immediately.

Water Parsley (Water Celery)
Treats five kinds of jaundice. For food-induced jaundice, take the juice and drink it, or boil and eat it, or eat the shoots raw. Use regularly as it is beneficial.

Green Onion (Fresh Scallion)
Treats injury [jaundice]. Extract the juice, fumigate with fragrant oil. Use both large and small green onions together. Heat thoroughly, remove the outer skin, burn and extract [the remedy].

Dongui Bogam, Miscellaneous Diseases Section, Volume 6

Open the patient's eyes and instill drops.

Empirical remedy: nosebleed — take chicken juice and drip it in.

Silkworm herb (絲草): Treats nosebleed. Prepare as yellow decoction; extract the juice and drink it.

White crow-hen (白烏雞): This refers to a white-headed young hen. For cold-damage with jaundice: remove the feathers, entrails, and urine [bladder]; chop finely with a knife; spread over the chest and head.

Bear bile (熊膽): Treats abscesses and epidemic febrile disease. Mix with yellow [medicine] and chive; extract and use.
